title.zh: 卷一百五十六 列傳第四十三: 董文炳 張弘範
title.en: Volume 156 Biographies 43: Dong Wenbing, Zhang Hongfan
title.raw: 卷一百五十六 列傳第四十三: 董文炳 張弘範 Volume 156 Biographies 43: Dong Wenbing, Zhang Hongfan

sentences.zh: 董文炳

translations.literal: Dong Wenbing
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenbing

sentences.zh: 董文炳字彥明，俊之長子也。

translations.literal: Dong Wenbing, courtesy name Yanming, was the eldest son of Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Wenbing, whose courtesy name was Yanming, was the eldest son of Dong Jun.

sentences.zh: 父歿時年始十六，率諸幼弟事母李夫人。

translations.literal: When his father died he was only sixteen; he led his younger brothers in serving their mother, Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he was only sixteen. He took charge of his younger brothers and together they attended their mother, Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 夫人有賢行，治家嚴，篤於教子。

translations.literal: The lady was virtuous in conduct, strict in managing the household, and devoted to educating her sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was known for her virtue, ran the household with strict discipline, and was deeply committed to her sons' education.

sentences.zh: 文炳師侍其先生，警敏善記誦，自幼儼如成人。

translations.literal: Wenbing studied under his teacher, was alert and clever and good at memorization, and from childhood conducted himself like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing studied with his teacher, showed a quick mind and a gift for memorization, and from boyhood carried himself with the gravity of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 歲乙未，以父任為藁城令。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year, through his father's appointment he became magistrate of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year (1235), he was appointed magistrate of Gaocheng on account of his father's position.

sentences.zh: 同列皆父時人，輕文炳年少，吏亦不之憚。

translations.literal: His colleagues were all men from his father's time; they looked down on Wenbing for his youth, and the clerks did not fear him either.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow officials were all veterans of his father's day. They dismissed Wenbing as too young, and the clerks showed him no respect.

sentences.zh: 文炳明於聽斷，以恩濟威。

translations.literal: Wenbing was skilled in hearing cases and rendering judgment, using kindness to temper severity.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing proved adept at hearing cases and passing judgment, tempering authority with mercy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，同列束手下之，吏抱案求署字，不敢仰視，里人亦大化服。

translations.literal: Before long his colleagues submitted to him; clerks would bring documents seeking his signature without daring to look up, and the villagers were also greatly reformed and won over.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his colleagues had submitted to him. Clerks would bring documents for his signature without daring to meet his eye, and the people of the district were thoroughly won over.

sentences.zh: 縣貧，重以旱蝗，而徵斂日暴，民不聊生。

translations.literal: The county was poor, compounded by drought and locusts, while levies grew daily more harsh, and the people could hardly survive.
translations.idiomatic: The county was poor to begin with, and drought and locusts made matters worse while levies grew harsher by the day. The people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 文炳以私穀數千石與縣，縣得以寬民。

translations.literal: Wenbing gave several thousand piculs of his private grain to the county, and the county was thereby able to ease the burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing contributed several thousand piculs of his own grain to the county treasury, enabling the magistracy to lighten the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: 前令因軍興乏用，稱貸於人，而貸家取息歲倍，縣以民蠶麥償之。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate, short of funds because of military campaigns, had borrowed on credit; the lenders charged interest doubling each year, and the county repaid them from the people's silk and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The previous magistrate, pressed for funds by the wars, had borrowed on credit at interest that doubled yearly, and the county had been repaying the lenders from the people's silk and wheat harvests.

sentences.zh: 文炳曰：「民困矣，吾為令，義不忍視也，吾當為代償。」

translations.literal: Wenbing said: "The people are in distress. As magistrate, I cannot in conscience look on; I shall repay it for them."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing said, "The people are suffering. As their magistrate, I cannot stand by and watch—I will repay the debt myself."

sentences.zh: 乃以田廬若干畝計直與貸家，復籍縣閒田與貧民為業，使耕之。

translations.literal: He then valued several dozen mu of fields and houses and gave them to the lenders, and also registered idle county land as property for the poor and had them cultivate it.
translations.idiomatic: He settled the debt by valuing several dozen mu of his own fields and homesteads and turning them over to the lenders. He also registered unused county land for poor families to farm as their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 於是流離漸還，數年間民食以足。

translations.literal: Thereupon the displaced gradually returned, and within a few years the people's food supply was sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced families gradually returned, and within a few years the people had enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初料民，令敢隱實者誅，籍其家。

translations.literal: When the court first assessed the population, it ordered that anyone who dared conceal the true count be executed and his household registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first conducted a population survey, it decreed death and confiscation of property for anyone who concealed the true household count.

sentences.zh: 文炳使民聚口而居，少為戶數。

translations.literal: Wenbing had the people live together in consolidated households, reducing the number of registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing had families consolidate into larger household units, thereby reducing the number of registered households.

sentences.zh: 衆以為不可，文炳曰：「為民獲罪，吾所甘心。」

translations.literal: The multitude thought this impossible; Wenbing said: "To incur guilt on the people's behalf is what I willingly accept."
translations.idiomatic: Many objected that this could not be done. Wenbing said, "If I must bear punishment on the people's behalf, I accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 民亦有不樂為者，文炳曰：「後當德我。」

translations.literal: Some among the people were also unwilling; Wenbing said: "Later you will be grateful to me."
translations.idiomatic: Some households were still reluctant. Wenbing told them, "You will thank me later."

sentences.zh: 由是賦斂大減，民皆富完。

translations.literal: Thereby levies were greatly reduced, and the people all became prosperous and secure.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, levies fell sharply, and the people grew prosperous and secure.

sentences.zh: 旁縣民有訟不得直者，皆詣文炳求決。

translations.literal: People of neighboring counties whose lawsuits could not obtain justice all came to Wenbing to seek judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants from neighboring counties who could not obtain a fair hearing all came to Wenbing for judgment.

sentences.zh: 文炳嘗上謁大府，旁縣人聚觀之，曰：「吾亟聞董令，董令顧亦人耳，何其明若神也！」

translations.literal: Wenbing once went up to pay respects at the superior prefecture; people from neighboring counties gathered to watch and said: "We have long heard of Magistrate Dong—Magistrate Dong is only a man after all; how can he be as clear-sighted as a spirit!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbing once went to the superior prefecture on official business, people from neighboring counties crowded around to watch and exclaimed, "We have heard so much of Magistrate Dong—and he is only a man! How can he judge with the clarity of a god?"

sentences.zh: 時府索無厭，文炳抑不予。

translations.literal: At that time the prefecture's demands were insatiable; Wenbing restrained and would not give in.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's demands were insatiable, but Wenbing held firm and refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 或讒之府，府欲中害之，文炳曰：「吾終不能剝民求利也。」

translations.literal: Some slandered him to the prefecture; the prefecture wished to harm him. Wenbing said: "I ultimately cannot strip the people to seek profit."
translations.idiomatic: Some maligned him to the prefecture, which sought to destroy him. Wenbing said, "I will never strip the people to fill official coffers."

sentences.zh: 即棄官去。

translations.literal: He immediately abandoned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his post at once and departed.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛藩，癸丑秋，受命憲宗征南詔。

translations.literal: When the future Shizu was in his princely domain, in the autumn of the guichou year, he received from Möngke the order for the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still in his princely domain, in the autumn of 1253 he received from Möngke Khan the order to campaign south.

sentences.zh: 文炳率義士四十六騎從行，人馬道死殆盡。

translations.literal: Wenbing led forty-six mounted volunteers in following the campaign; men and horses died on the road until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing led forty-six mounted volunteers on the march. Men and horses perished along the way until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 及至吐番，止兩人能從，兩人者挾文炳徒行，躑躅道路，取死馬肉續食，日行不能三二十里，然志益厲，期必至軍。

translations.literal: When they reached Tibet, only two men could still follow; the two supported Wenbing on foot, hobbling along the road, eating the flesh of dead horses to sustain themselves, unable to cover twenty or thirty li a day, yet his resolve grew firmer, determined to reach the army.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Tibet, only two companions remained. They supported Wenbing on foot, stumbling along the road and eating the flesh of dead horses to stay alive. They could manage barely twenty or thirty li a day, yet his resolve only hardened—he was determined to reach the army.

sentences.zh: 會使者過，遇文炳，還言其狀。

translations.literal: It happened that a messenger passed by, met Wenbing, and returned to report his condition.
translations.idiomatic: A courier happened to pass by, met Wenbing, and returned to report his plight.

sentences.zh: 時文炳弟文忠先從世祖軍，世祖即命文忠解尚五馬載糗糧迎文炳。

translations.literal: At that time Wenbing's younger brother Wenzhong had already followed the prince's army; the prince immediately ordered Wenzhong to take five saddled horses carrying dry rations to meet Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing's younger brother Wenzhong was already with Kublai's army. The prince at once ordered Wenzhong to take five saddled horses loaded with provisions to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既至，世祖壯其忠，且閔其勞，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the prince admired his loyalty and pitied his hardships, bestowing rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Kublai admired his loyalty and pitied his ordeal, rewarding him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 有任使皆稱旨，由是日親貴用事。

translations.literal: Whatever mission he was given accorded with the prince's intent; from this he daily grew close, honored, and influential.
translations.idiomatic: Every task entrusted to him met with the prince's approval, and from that day he grew ever closer, honored, and influential at court.

sentences.zh: 己未秋，世祖伐宋，至淮西臺山寨，命文炳往取之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the jiwei year, the prince attacked Song, reaching Taishan Stockade in western Huai, and ordered Wenbing to go take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1259, Kublai marched against Song and reached Taishan Stockade in western Huai. He ordered Wenbing to capture it.

sentences.zh: 文炳馳至寨下，諭以禍福，不應，文炳脫冑呼曰：「吾所以不極兵威者，欲活汝衆也，不速下，今屠寨矣。」

translations.literal: Wenbing galloped to below the stockade and admonished them with fortune and disaster; they did not respond. Wenbing removed his helmet and shouted: "The reason I have not brought full military force to bear is that I wish to spare your multitude. If you do not surrender quickly, I shall slaughter the stockade now."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing rode to the foot of the stockade and urged them with talk of consequences, but they would not answer. He took off his helmet and shouted, "I have held back my full force because I want you to live. Surrender at once, or I will slaughter every soul in this stockade."

sentences.zh: 守者懼，遂降。

translations.literal: The defenders were afraid and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders were terrified and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 九月，師次陽羅堡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army halted at Yangluo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army encamped at Yangluo Fort.

sentences.zh: 宋兵築堡于岸，陳船江中，軍容甚盛，文炳請於世祖曰：「長江天險，宋所恃以為國，勢必死守，不奪其氣不可，臣請嘗之。」

translations.literal: Song troops had built a fort on the bank and arrayed ships in the river; their military appearance was very imposing. Wenbing requested of the prince: "The Yangtze is heaven's barrier, what Song relies on as its state—they are sure to defend it to the death. Their spirit cannot be taken without trying; your servant asks to test it."
translations.idiomatic: Song forces had built a fort on the shore and lined warships across the river in an imposing display. Wenbing said to Kublai, "The Yangtze is Song's natural fortress and the foundation of their state. They will fight to the death here—we must break their morale, and I ask leave to make the first trial."

sentences.zh: 即與敢死士數十百人當其前，率弟文用、文忠，載艨艟鼓櫂疾趨，叫呼畢奮。

translations.literal: He immediately took several hundred dare-to-die troops to face them at the front, leading his younger brothers Wenyong and Wenzhong, loading tower ships and beating oars in swift advance, shouting and then charging with full force.
translations.idiomatic: He took several hundred volunteers to the fore, leading his brothers Wenyong and Wenzhong in tower ships with drums beating and oars driving hard. They shouted themselves hoarse, then charged with everything they had.

sentences.zh: 鋒既交，文炳麾衆趨岸搏之，宋師大敗。

translations.literal: Once the vanguards clashed, Wenbing directed the troops to rush ashore and grapple with them; the Song army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguards met, Wenbing drove his men ashore to grapple at close quarters, and the Song army was routed.

sentences.zh: 命文用輕舟報捷。

translations.literal: He ordered Wenyong in a light boat to report the victory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wenyong in a light boat to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 世祖方駐香爐峰，因策馬下山問戰勝狀，則扶鞍起立，豎鞭仰指曰：「天也！」

translations.literal: The prince was then encamped at Incense Burner Peak; hearing this he spurred his horse down the mountain to ask how the battle had been won, then braced himself on the saddle and stood, raising his whip and pointing upward, saying: "Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was encamped on Incense Burner Peak. He rode down the mountain to ask how the battle had been won, then braced himself on the saddle, raised his whip toward the sky, and cried, "Heaven itself has willed this!"

sentences.zh: 且命他師毋解甲，明日將圍城。

translations.literal: He also ordered the other divisions not to remove their armor; the next day they would besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the other divisions to keep their armor on—the city would be besieged the next day.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，會憲宗崩。

translations.literal: After crossing the river, it happened that Möngke died.
translations.idiomatic: After the army crossed the river, Möngke Khan died.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，班師。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年，李璮反濟南。

translations.literal: In the third year, Li Tan rebelled at Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1262), Li Tan rebelled at Jinan.

sentences.zh: 璮劇賊，善用兵。

translations.literal: Tan was a fierce rebel and skilled in using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was a formidable rebel and a skilled commander.

sentences.zh: 文炳會諸軍圍之，璮不得遁。

translations.literal: Wenbing joined the various armies in besieging him, and Tan could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing joined the allied armies in besieging him, and Tan could not break out.

sentences.zh: 久之，賊勢日蹙，文炳曰：「窮寇可以計擒。」

translations.literal: After a long time the rebel force grew daily more pressed; Wenbing said: "A cornered bandit can be taken by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: As the siege wore on, the rebels grew weaker by the day. Wenbing said, "A cornered enemy can be taken by strategy."

sentences.zh: 乃抵城下，呼璮將田都帥者曰：「反者璮耳，餘來即吾人，毋自取死也。」

translations.literal: He then reached below the city wall and called to Tan's general known as Commander Tian: "The rebel is Tan alone; the rest of you who come over are our people—do not bring death on yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: He went to the foot of the wall and called to Tan's general, Commander Tian: "Only Tan is the rebel. The rest of you are our people once you come over—do not throw your lives away."

sentences.zh: 田縋城降。

translations.literal: Tian was lowered from the wall by rope and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was lowered over the wall by rope and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 田，璮之愛將，既降，衆遂亂，禽璮以獻。

translations.literal: Tian was Tan's favorite general; once he surrendered, the multitude fell into disorder, and Tan was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was Tan's favorite commander. Once he surrendered, the rebel ranks collapsed, and Tan was captured and brought in.

sentences.zh: 璮兵有浙、漣兩軍二萬餘人，勇而善戰，主將怒其與賊，配諸軍，使陰殺之。

translations.literal: Tan's troops included more than twenty thousand men of the Zhe and Lian armies, brave and skilled in battle; the commander-in-chief, angry that they had sided with the rebel, distributed them among the various armies to have them secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's forces included more than twenty thousand troops of the Zhe and Lian armies—brave and formidable fighters. The commander-in-chief, furious that they had sided with the rebel, scattered them among other units to be killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 文炳當殺二千人，言于主將曰：「彼為璮所脅耳，殺之恐乖天子仁聖之意。

translations.literal: Wenbing was to kill two thousand men; he said to the commander-in-chief: "They were coerced by Tan alone; to kill them would likely run counter to the Son of Heaven's benevolent and sagely intent.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand men were assigned to Wenbing for execution. He told the commander-in-chief, "They were coerced by Tan alone. To kill them would betray the Son of Heaven's benevolent purpose.

sentences.zh: 向天子伐南詔，或妄殺人，雖大將亦罪之，是不宜殺也。」

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven campaigned against Nanzhao, if anyone killed people without cause, even great generals were punished—therefore they should not be killed."
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven campaigned against Nanzhao, even senior generals were punished for killing without cause. These men should not be killed."

sentences.zh: 主將從之。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief agreed.

sentences.zh: 然他殺之者已衆，皆大悔。

translations.literal: Yet those killed by others were already numerous, and all greatly regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: But many had already been killed elsewhere, and all deeply regretted it.

sentences.zh: 璮伏誅，山東猶未靖，乃以文炳為山東東路經略使，率親軍以行。

translations.literal: After Tan was executed, Shandong was still not pacified; Wenbing was therefore made Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern Route in Shandong and led his personal army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After Tan was executed, Shandong remained unsettled. Wenbing was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern Route in Shandong and led his personal troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 出金銀符五十，有功者聽與之。

translations.literal: He issued fifty gold and silver tallies, granting them to whoever had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He issued fifty gold and silver commendation tallies to reward those who distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 閏九月，文炳至益都，留兵于外，從數騎衣冠而入。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month Wenbing reached Yidu, left troops outside, and with only a few mounted followers entered in full official dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month Wenbing reached Yidu. He left his troops outside and entered the city with only a few mounted attendants, dressed in full official regalia.

sentences.zh: 居府，不設警衛，召璮故將吏立之庭，曰：「璮狂賊，詿誤汝等。

translations.literal: He took up residence in the government compound without setting guards, summoned Tan's former generals and officials to stand in the courtyard, and said: "Tan was a mad rebel who misled you.
translations.idiomatic: He took up residence in the government compound without posting guards, summoned Tan's former officers to the courtyard, and said, "Tan was a mad rebel who led you astray.

sentences.zh: 璮已誅死，汝皆為王民，天子至仁聖，遣經略使撫汝，當相安毋懼。

translations.literal: Tan has already been executed; you are all subjects of the king. The Son of Heaven is supremely benevolent and sagely and has sent the pacification commissioner to comfort you—you should live in peace and not fear.
translations.idiomatic: Tan is dead. You are all subjects of the throne. The Son of Heaven is supremely benevolent and has sent me to reassure you. Live in peace and have no fear.

sentences.zh: 經略使得便宜除擬將吏，汝等勉取金銀符，經略使不敢格上命不予有功者。」

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner may provisionally appoint and remove generals and officials at discretion; strive to earn the gold and silver tallies—the pacification commissioner dares not block the court's orders and withhold them from the meritorious."
translations.idiomatic: As pacification commissioner I may appoint and promote officers at my discretion. Do your best to earn the commendation tallies—I will not withhold them from anyone who deserves them."

sentences.zh: 所部大悅，山東以安。

translations.literal: His subordinates were greatly pleased, and Shandong was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates were greatly reassured, and Shandong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，帝懲李璮之亂，欲潛銷方鎮之橫，以文炳代史氏兩萬戶為鄧州光化行軍萬戶、河南等路統軍副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, the emperor, taking warning from Li Tan's rebellion and wishing secretly to dissolve the overweening power of regional commanders, replaced the Shi clan's two ten-thousand-household units with Wenbing as Military Ten-Thousand-Household of Dengzhou and Guanghua on campaign and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Henan and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1266, taking warning from Li Tan's rebellion and seeking quietly to curb the power of regional military governors, the emperor replaced the Shi clan's two ten-thousand-household commands with Wenbing, appointing him Military Ten-Thousand-Household of Dengzhou and Guanghua on campaign and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Henan and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 到官，造戰艦五百艘，習水戰，預謀取宋方略，凡阨塞要害皆列柵築堡，為備禦計。

translations.literal: On taking office he built five hundred warships, practiced naval warfare, and planned in advance the strategy for taking Song; wherever passes and strategic points were chokepoints he set up palisades and built forts as defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he built five hundred warships and trained his forces in naval warfare, planning the strategy for conquering Song in advance. At every pass and strategic point he erected palisades and built forts as defensive measures.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗召文炳密謀，欲大發河北民丁。

translations.literal: The emperor once summoned Wenbing for secret counsel, intending to levy a great draft of militia from Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once summoned Wenbing for secret counsel, intending to levy a massive draft of militia from Hebei.

sentences.zh: 文炳曰：「河南密邇宋境，人習江淮地利，宜使河北耕以供軍，河南戰以辟地。

translations.literal: Wenbing said: "Henan borders Song territory closely; its people are practiced in the terrain and advantages of the Jiang-Huai region. It is fitting to have Hebei farm to supply the army and Henan fight to open territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing said, "Henan lies close to Song territory, and its people know the Jiang-Huai terrain. Let Hebei farm to supply the armies and Henan fight to expand our holdings.

sentences.zh: 俟宋平，則河北長隸兵籍，河南削籍為民。

translations.literal: When Song is pacified, then Hebei may long remain on the military registers and Henan be struck from the registers and made civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Once Song is pacified, Hebei can remain on the military rolls permanently while Henan is removed from the rolls and restored to civilian status.

sentences.zh: 如是為便。

translations.literal: Thus would be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: That would be the most practical arrangement.

sentences.zh: 又將校素無俸給，連年用兵，至有身為大校出無馬乘者。

translations.literal: Moreover, officers and commanders had never had stipends; after years of campaigning, there were even men who as senior commanders went out with no horse to ride.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, officers had never received regular pay. After years of campaigning, some senior commanders had no horse even to ride on campaign.

sentences.zh: 臣即所部千戶私役兵士四人，百戶二人，聽其雇役，稍食其力。」

translations.literal: Your servant would allow each thousand-household unit under his command four soldiers for private service and each hundred-household unit two, permitting them to hire them out and thereby slightly benefit from their labor."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that each thousand-household unit under my command be allowed four soldiers for private hire and each hundred-household unit two, so they may earn a modest income from their labor."

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之，始頒將校俸錢，以秩為差。

translations.literal: The emperor followed all his proposals and for the first time issued pay to officers and commanders, graded by rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all his proposals and for the first time instituted regular pay for officers, graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 七年，改山東路統軍副使，治沂州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was changed to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Shandong Route and administered Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1270) he was transferred to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Shandong Route, with his headquarters at Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 沂與宋接境，鎮兵仰內郡餉運。

translations.literal: Yi bordered Song territory; the garrison troops relied on grain transport from the interior prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou bordered Song territory, and the garrison depended on grain shipments from interior prefectures.

sentences.zh: 有詔和糴本部，文炳命收州縣所移文。

translations.literal: There was an edict for coordinated grain purchase within his jurisdiction; Wenbing ordered the documents forwarded from prefectures and counties to be collected.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered coordinated grain purchases within his jurisdiction. Wenbing had the documents from prefectures and counties collected and withheld.

sentences.zh: 衆諫以違詔，文炳曰：「但止之。」

translations.literal: The multitude admonished him for violating the edict; Wenbing said: "Simply stop it."
translations.idiomatic: His staff warned that this defied the edict. Wenbing said, "Just stop it for now."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使入奏，略曰：「敵人接壤，知吾虛實，一不可；

translations.literal: He then sent a messenger to memorialize the throne, stating in summary: "The enemy borders us and would learn our strengths and weaknesses—first, this cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: He sent a messenger to memorialize the throne, arguing in brief: "First, the enemy borders us and would learn our strengths and weaknesses;

sentences.zh: 邊民供頓甚勞，重苦此役，二不可；

translations.literal: the border people are greatly wearied in supplying provisions, and this levy would doubly afflict them—second, this cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: second, the border people are already exhausted supplying the army, and this levy would crush them further;

sentences.zh: 困吾民以懼來者，三不可。」

translations.literal: to distress our people and frighten those who would come after—third, this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: third, to impoverish our own people would only discourage future settlers."

sentences.zh: 帝大悟，罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enlightened and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was fully persuaded and canceled the order.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷樞密院判官，行院事於淮西。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and conducted the bureau's affairs in western Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1272) he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and directed its affairs in western Huai.

sentences.zh: 築正陽兩城，兩城夾淮相望，以綴襄陽及擣宋腹心。

translations.literal: He built the two cities of Zhengyang; the two cities faced each other across the Huai to pin down Xiangyang and strike at Song's heartland.
translations.idiomatic: He built the twin cities of Zhengyang on opposite banks of the Huai to pin down Xiangyang and threaten Song's heartland.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1273) he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夏，霖雨，水漲，宋淮西制置使夏貴帥舟師十萬來攻，矢石雨下，文炳登城禦之。

translations.literal: In summer, prolonged rain fell and the waters rose; Song's Pacification Commissioner of Western Huai, Xia Gui, led a fleet of one hundred thousand to attack; arrows and stones rained down; Wenbing mounted the wall to defend.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, weeks of rain swelled the rivers. Song's Pacification Commissioner of Western Huai, Xia Gui, led a fleet of one hundred thousand warships to attack. Arrows and stones rained down as Wenbing mounted the wall to direct the defense.

sentences.zh: 一夕，貴去復來，飛矢貫文炳左臂，著脅。

translations.literal: One night Gui withdrew and returned; a flying arrow pierced Wenbing's left arm and lodged in his side.
translations.idiomatic: One night Xia Gui withdrew, then returned. A stray arrow pierced Wenbing's left arm and lodged in his ribs.

sentences.zh: 文炳拔矢授左右，發四十餘矢。

translations.literal: Wenbing pulled out the arrow and handed it to an attendant, then shot more than forty arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing pulled out the arrow, handed it to an attendant, and shot more than forty arrows in return.

sentences.zh: 菔中矢盡，顧左右索矢，又十餘發，矢不繼，力亦困，不能張滿，遂悶絕幾殆。

translations.literal: When the arrows in his sleeve were exhausted, he looked to his attendants for arrows and shot more than ten; arrows did not follow, his strength was also spent, and he could not draw the bow full—thereupon he fainted and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: When his quiver was empty he called for more and shot another dozen, but arrows ran out and his strength failed—he could no longer draw the bow fully and collapsed, nearly dead.

sentences.zh: 明日，水入外郭，文炳麾士卒欲避，貴乘之，壓軍而陣。

translations.literal: The next day water entered the outer wall; Wenbing directed the troops to withdraw; Gui seized the moment, pressed the army forward, and formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: The next day floodwaters breached the outer wall. Wenbing ordered his troops to withdraw, but Xia Gui pressed the attack and deployed his army in battle formation.

sentences.zh: 文炳病創甚，子士選請代戰，文炳壯而遣之，復自起束創，手劍督戰。

translations.literal: Wenbing's wound was very severe; his son Shixuan asked to fight in his place; Wenbing admired this and sent him; he himself rose again, bound his wound, and with sword in hand supervised the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing's wound was grave. His son Shixuan volunteered to fight in his stead. Wenbing, impressed, sent him out, then rose himself, bound his wound, and took up his sword to direct the battle.

sentences.zh: 士選以戈擊貴將仆，不死，獲之以獻。

translations.literal: Shixuan struck one of Gui's generals with a halberd and knocked him down; he did not die but was captured and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan struck down one of Xia Gui's generals with a halberd. Though the man did not die, he was captured and brought before Wenbing.

sentences.zh: 貴遂去，不敢復來。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon departed and did not dare return.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui withdrew and did not dare return.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大舉兵伐宋，丞相伯顏自襄陽東下，與宋人戰陽羅堡。

translations.literal: That year a great army was raised to attack Song; the Chancellor Bayan marched east from Xiangyang and fought the Song at Yangluo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court launched a major campaign against Song. Chancellor Bayan marched east from Xiangyang and fought the Song at Yangluo Fort.

sentences.zh: 文炳以九月發正陽，十一年正月會伯顏于安慶。

translations.literal: Wenbing set out from Zhengyang in the ninth month; in the first month of the eleventh year he joined Bayan at Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing set out from Zhengyang in the ninth month and joined Bayan at Anqing in the first month of the eleventh year (1274).

sentences.zh: 安慶守將范文虎以城降。

translations.literal: Anqing's defending general Fan Wenhui surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing's defender Fan Wenhui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 文炳請于伯顏曰：「大軍既疲於陽羅堡，吾兵當前行。」

translations.literal: Wenbing requested of Bayan: "The great army is already wearied from Yangluo Fort; our troops should advance first."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing said to Bayan, "Your main force is exhausted from Yangluo Fort. My troops should take the lead."

sentences.zh: 伯顏許之。

translations.literal: Bayan granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan agreed.

sentences.zh: 宋都督賈似道來禦，師陳於蕪湖，似道棄師走。

translations.literal: Song's Commander-in-Chief Jia Sidao came to resist; the army formed lines at Wuhu; Sidao abandoned his troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Commander-in-Chief Jia Sidao came to resist, but when the armies faced each other at Wuhu, Sidao abandoned his troops and fled.

sentences.zh: 次當塗，文炳復言于伯顏曰：「采石當江之南，和州對峙，不取，必有後顧。」

translations.literal: Halting at Dangtu, Wenbing again said to Bayan: "Caishi lies south of the river and Hezhou faces it across the stream; if we do not take them, we are sure to have concerns behind us."
translations.idiomatic: At Dangtu, Wenbing again urged Bayan: "Caishi lies south of the river with Hezhou facing it across the stream. If we do not take them, we will always be looking over our shoulder."

sentences.zh: 遂進攻之，降知州事王喜。

translations.literal: He thereupon advanced to attack them and received the surrender of Prefect Wang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to attack, and Prefect Wang Xi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三月，有詔以時向暑熱，命伯顏軍駐建康，文炳軍駐鎮江。

translations.literal: In the third month an edict, noting that the season was turning hot, ordered Bayan's army to encamp at Jiankang and Wenbing's army at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an edict, citing the approaching summer heat, ordered Bayan's army to encamp at Jiankang and Wenbing's at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 時揚州、真州堅守不下，常州、蘇州既降復叛。

translations.literal: At that time Yangzhou and Zhenzhou held firm and would not fall, while Changzhou and Suzhou had surrendered but rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou and Zhenzhou still held out stubbornly, while Changzhou and Suzhou, having surrendered once, rose in rebellion again.

sentences.zh: 張世傑、孫虎臣約真、揚兵誓死戰，真、揚兵戰每敗，不敢出。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen joined with the troops of Zhen and Yang in a sworn fight to the death; the Zhen and Yang troops were defeated in every battle and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen rallied the Zhen and Yang garrisons to fight to the death, but those troops were beaten in every engagement and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 世傑等陳大艦萬艘，碇焦山下江中，勁卒居前。

translations.literal: Shijie and the others arrayed ten thousand great ships, anchoring at Jiaoshan below in the river, with crack troops posted in front.
translations.idiomatic: They deployed ten thousand large warships, anchoring at Jiaoshan in the river with elite troops in the van.

sentences.zh: 文炳身犯之，載士選別船。

translations.literal: Wenbing personally braved the attack, placing Shixuan on a separate ship.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing led the assault in person, with Shixuan aboard a separate vessel.

sentences.zh: 弟之子士表請從，文炳顧曰：「吾弟僅汝一子，脫吾與士選不返，士元、士秀猶足殺敵，吾不忍汝往也。」

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Shibiao asked to follow; Wenbing looked at him and said: "My brother has only you as a son. If I and Shixuan do not return, Shiyuan and Shixiu are still enough to kill the enemy—I cannot bear for you to go."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Shibiao asked to join him. Wenbing said, "Your father has only you. If Shixuan and I do not return, Shiyuan and Shixiu can still fight—but I cannot send you into this."

sentences.zh: 士表固請，乃許。

translations.literal: Shibiao pressed his request firmly and was thereupon permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao pressed his case until Wenbing relented.

sentences.zh: 文炳乘輪船，建大將旗鼓，士選、士表船翼之，大呼突陣，諸將繼進，飛矢蔽日。

translations.literal: Wenbing boarded a paddle-wheel ship, raised the great general's banners and drums; Shixuan and Shibiao's ships flanked him; he shouted and charged the formation; the generals followed; flying arrows blotted out the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing took a paddle-wheel warship under the great general's banners and drums, with Shixuan and Shibiao flanking him. He charged the enemy line with a great shout as the other generals pressed forward and arrows darkened the sky.

sentences.zh: 戰酣，短兵相接，宋兵亦殊死戰，聲震天地，橫屍委仗，江水為之不流。

translations.literal: As the battle grew fierce, close combat ensued; Song troops also fought to the death; the sound shook heaven and earth; corpses lay across abandoned weapons, and the river water ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting grew desperate at close quarters. Song troops fought with equal fury until the din shook heaven and earth. Corpses and abandoned weapons littered the field, and the river seemed to stand still.

sentences.zh: 自寅至午，宋師大敗，世傑走，文炳追及于夾灘。

translations.literal: From the hour of yin to the hour of wu the Song army was greatly defeated; Shijie fled; Wenbing overtook him at Jiatan.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn to midday the Song army was routed. Shijie fled, and Wenbing caught up with him at Jiatan.

sentences.zh: 世傑收潰卒復戰，又破之，遂東走於海。

translations.literal: Shijie gathered the routed troops and fought again; they were defeated once more; he thereupon fled eastward onto the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie rallied his broken forces and fought again, only to be defeated once more. He fled eastward onto the sea.

sentences.zh: 文炳船小，不可入海，夜乃還。

translations.literal: Wenbing's ships were small and could not enter the sea; at night he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing's ships were too small to pursue onto the open sea, and he returned that night.

sentences.zh: 俘甲士萬餘人，悉縱不殺，獲戰船七百艘，宋力自此遂窮。

translations.literal: He captured more than ten thousand armored soldiers and released them all without killing; he obtained seven hundred warships; Song's strength was thereby exhausted from this point.
translations.idiomatic: He took more than ten thousand armored soldiers prisoner and released them all unharmed. He captured seven hundred warships, and Song's military power was broken from that day forward.

sentences.zh: 十月，諸軍分三道而進，文炳居左，由江並海趨臨安。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the armies advanced in three columns; Wenbing was on the left, proceeding along the river and by sea toward Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the armies advanced in three columns. Wenbing commanded the left wing, marching along the river and coast toward Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 先是，江陰軍僉判李世修欲降不果，文炳檄諭之，世修以城來附，令權本軍安撫使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Shixiu, military judge of Jiangyin, had wished to surrender but failed; Wenbing issued a proclamation admonishing him; Shixiu came with the city to submit, and was appointed acting Pacification Commissioner of that army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Shixiu, deputy military judge of Jiangyin, had tried to surrender without success. Wenbing sent a proclamation urging him on, and Shixiu submitted the city. Wenbing appointed him acting Pacification Commissioner of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 所過民不知兵，凡獲生口，悉縱遣之，無敢匿者，威信前布，皆望旗而服。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed the people did not know war; all captives taken were released and sent away; none dared conceal themselves; his authority and trust spread ahead, and all submitted at sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched, the people scarcely knew an army had passed. Every captive was released, none dared hide, and his reputation preceded him so that all submitted at sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 張瑄有衆數千，負海為橫，文炳命招討使王世強及士選往降之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuan had several thousand followers and defied the sea coast; Wenbing ordered Pacification Commissioner Wang Shiqiang and Shixuan to go and induce his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan commanded several thousand men and dominated the coast. Wenbing sent Pacification Commissioner Wang Shiqiang and Shixuan to accept his surrender.

sentences.zh: 士選單舸至瑄所，諭以威德，瑄降，得海舶五百。

translations.literal: Shixuan went alone in a single boat to Xuan's place, admonished him with authority and virtue; Xuan surrendered, and five hundred seagoing vessels were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan went alone in a small boat to Zhang Xuan's camp and persuaded him with talk of power and mercy. Xuan surrendered, yielding five hundred seagoing vessels.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月，次鹽官。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the thirteenth year he halted at Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the thirteenth year (1276) he halted at Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 鹽官，臨安劇縣，俟救至，招之再返不下。

translations.literal: Yanguan was a strategic county of Lin'an; awaiting relief forces, it was summoned repeatedly but would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguan was a key county near Lin'an. Awaiting relief, it was summoned repeatedly but refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 將佐請屠之，文炳曰：「縣去臨安不百里，聲勢相及，臨安約降已有成言，吾輕殺一人，則害大計，況屠一縣耶。」

translations.literal: Generals and aides asked to slaughter it; Wenbing said: "The county is less than a hundred li from Lin'an; their situations affect each other; Lin'an's agreed surrender already has settled terms—if I lightly kill one man I harm the great plan, how much more slaughtering a whole county?"
translations.idiomatic: His officers asked to slaughter the county. Wenbing said, "Yanguan lies less than a hundred li from Lin'an, and their fates are linked. Lin'an has already agreed to surrender—if I kill one man lightly I ruin the larger plan, let alone massacre an entire county."

sentences.zh: 於是遣人入城諭意，縣降。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent men into the city to convey his intent, and the county surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys into the city to explain his intentions, and the county surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂會伯顏于臨安城北。

translations.literal: He thereupon joined Bayan north of Lin'an city.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Bayan north of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 張世傑欲以其主逃之海，文炳繞出臨安城南，戍浙江亭。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie wished to take his lord and flee to the sea; Wenbing circled out south of Lin'an city and garrisoned Zhejiang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie planned to flee with the Song emperor by sea. Wenbing swung south of Lin'an and garrisoned Zhejiang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 世傑計不行，乃竊宋主弟吉王昰、廣王昞南走，而宋主遂降。

translations.literal: Shijie's plan could not be carried out; he thereupon secretly took the Song ruler's younger brothers, Prince Ji Zhao and Prince Guang Zhao, and fled south, while the Song ruler thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie's plan failed. He secretly fled south with the Song emperor's younger brothers, Princes Ji and Guang, while the Song emperor himself surrendered.

sentences.zh: 伯顏命文炳入城，罷宋官府，散其諸軍，封庫藏，收禮樂器及諸圖籍。

translations.literal: Bayan ordered Wenbing to enter the city, abolish Song government offices, disband its armies, seal the treasuries, and collect ritual instruments and all maps and records.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan ordered Wenbing into the city to abolish Song government offices, disband the armies, seal the treasuries, and collect ritual instruments, maps, and archives.

sentences.zh: 文炳取宋主諸璽符上於伯顏。

translations.literal: Wenbing took all the Song ruler's seals and tallies and presented them to Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing collected the Song emperor's seals and tallies and presented them to Bayan.

sentences.zh: 伯顏以宋主入覲，有詔留事一委文炳。

translations.literal: Bayan took the Song ruler to court audience; an edict left all remaining affairs entirely to Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan escorted the Song emperor to court. An edict left all remaining affairs entirely in Wenbing's hands.

sentences.zh: 禁戢豪猾，無慰士女，宋民不知易主。

translations.literal: He prohibited and restrained the powerful and unruly, comforted scholars and common people, and Song subjects did not know their ruler had changed.
translations.idiomatic: He restrained the powerful and lawless, reassured scholars and commoners, and the people of Song scarcely realized their dynasty had changed.

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士李槃奉詔招宋士至臨安，文炳謂之曰：「國可滅，史不可沒。

translations.literal: At that time Hanlin Academician Li Pan was ordered to summon Song scholars to Lin'an; Wenbing said to him: "A state may be destroyed, but history must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Li Pan was then ordered to summon Song scholars to Lin'an. Wenbing told him, "A state may fall, but its history must not perish.

sentences.zh: 宋十六主，有天下三百餘年，其太史所記具在史館，宜悉收以備典禮。」

translations.literal: Song had sixteen rulers and held the realm for more than three hundred years; what the grand historians recorded is all in the history archives—it is fitting to collect it all to prepare the canonical rites."
translations.idiomatic: Song had sixteen rulers and held the realm for more than three hundred years. Everything the court historians recorded is in the archives—you must collect it all for the rites of state."

sentences.zh: 乃得宋史及諸注記五千餘冊，歸之國史院。

translations.literal: He thereby obtained more than five thousand volumes of Song history and various commentaries and records, and returned them to the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered more than five thousand volumes of Song histories and commentaries and deposited them in the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 宋宗室福王與芮赴京師，遍以重寶致諸貴人，文炳獨却不受。

translations.literal: Song imperial clansman Prince Fu Zhao Ru went to the capital and everywhere presented heavy treasures to the nobles; Wenbing alone refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Song prince Zhao Ru went to the capital and lavished costly gifts on every noble he met. Wenbing alone refused them.

sentences.zh: 及官錄與芮家。

translations.literal: When officials recorded Zhao Ru's household.
translations.idiomatic: When officials later inventoried Zhao Ru's household gifts,

sentences.zh: 具籍受寶者，惟文炳無名。

translations.literal: Those listed in full registers as receiving treasures—only Wenbing had no name.
translations.idiomatic: the register of recipients listed every name but Wenbing's.

sentences.zh: 伯顏入朝奏曰：「臣等奉天威平宋，宋既已平，懷徠安集之功，董文炳居多。」

translations.literal: Bayan entered court and memorialized: "Your servants, bearing heaven's majesty, pacified Song; now that Song is pacified, the merit in winning hearts and settling the realm lies mostly with Dong Wenbing."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan reported to court: "We bore heaven's authority to pacify Song. Now that Song is pacified, the work of winning hearts and securing the realm belongs chiefly to Dong Wenbing."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「文炳吾舊臣，忠勤朕所素知。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wenbing is my old minister; his loyalty and diligence are what I have always known."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wenbing is an old servant of mine. His loyalty and diligence have never been in doubt."

sentences.zh: 乃拜資德大夫、中書左丞。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時張世傑奉吉王昰據台州，而閩中亦為宋守。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shijie supported Prince Ji Zhao and held Taizhou, while Fujian also remained in Song hands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie still held Taizhou with Prince Ji Zhao, and Fujian also remained loyal to Song.

sentences.zh: 敕文炳進兵，所過禁士馬無敢履踐田麥，曰：「在倉者吾既食之，在野者汝又踐之，新邑之民何以續命。」

translations.literal: Wenbing was ordered to advance; wherever he passed he forbade soldiers and horses from treading on the wheat in the fields, saying: "What is in the granaries we have already eaten—if you also trample what is in the fields, how are the people of these new territories to sustain their lives?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing was ordered to advance. He forbade troops and horses to trample the wheat in the fields, saying, "We have already eaten what is in the granaries—if you trample what grows in the fields, how will the people of these new territories survive?"

sentences.zh: 是以南人感之，不忍以兵相向。

translations.literal: Therefore the people of the south were moved by him and could not bear to oppose him with arms.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the south were so moved that they could not bring themselves to take up arms against him.

sentences.zh: 次台州，世傑遁。

translations.literal: Halting at Taizhou, Shijie fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizhou, Shijie fled.

sentences.zh: 諸將先俘州民，文炳下令曰：「台人首效順於我，我不暇有，故世傑據之，其民何罪。

translations.literal: The generals had first taken the prefecture's people captive; Wenbing issued an order: "The people of Taizhou were the first to submit to us—we had no leisure to take possession, and therefore Shijie held it; what crime have its people committed?
translations.idiomatic: The generals had already taken Taizhou's people captive. Wenbing ordered, "Taizhou was the first to submit to us—we had no time to secure it, and so Shijie seized it. What crime have its people committed?

sentences.zh: 敢有不縱所俘者，以軍法論。」

translations.literal: Whoever dares not release those captured will be dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who fails to release the captives will be punished under military law."

sentences.zh: 得免者數萬口。

translations.literal: Those spared numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands were spared.

sentences.zh: 至溫州，溫州未下，令曰：「毋取子女，毋掠民有。」

translations.literal: Reaching Wenzhou, which had not yet fallen, he ordered: "Do not take sons and daughters, do not plunder what the people possess."
translations.idiomatic: At Wenzhou, which had not yet fallen, he ordered, "Take no children, seize no private property."

sentences.zh: 衆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: The troops said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: The troops answered, "Yes, sir."

sentences.zh: 其守將火城中逃，文炳亟命滅火，追擒其將，數其殘民之罪，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Its defending general set fire to the city and fled; Wenbing urgently ordered the fire extinguished, pursued and captured the general, enumerated his crimes of harming the people, and executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general set the city ablaze and fled. Wenbing ordered the fire put out at once, pursued and captured the general, condemned him for harming the people, and executed him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 逾嶺，閩人扶老來迎，漳、泉、建寧、邵武諸郡皆送款來附。

translations.literal: Crossing the mountains, Fujian people supported the elderly in coming to welcome him; the prefectures of Zhang, Quan, Jianning, and Shaowu all sent tokens of submission to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the mountains into Fujian, the people came out to welcome him, the old supported on the arms of the young. Zhang, Quan, Jianning, Shaowu, and other prefectures all submitted.

sentences.zh: 凡得州若干、縣若干、戶口若干。

translations.literal: In all he obtained so many prefectures, so many counties, and so many households.
translations.idiomatic: He secured a substantial number of prefectures, counties, and registered households.

sentences.zh: 閩人感文炳德最深，廟而祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian were most deeply moved by Wenbing's virtue and built temples to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian revered Wenbing's kindness above all and built temples in his honor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，帝在上都，適北邊有警，欲親將北伐。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the emperor was at Shangdu; it happened that there was an alarm on the northern frontier, and he wished to lead a northern campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1277) the emperor was at Shangdu. Trouble on the northern frontier prompted him to lead a campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 正月，急召文炳。

translations.literal: In the first month he urgently summoned Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month he urgently summoned Wenbing.

sentences.zh: 四月，文炳至自臨安。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Wenbing arrived from Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wenbing arrived from Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 比至，帝日問來期。

translations.literal: As he approached, the emperor daily asked when he would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: As he drew near, the emperor asked daily when he would arrive.

sentences.zh: 及至，即召入。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was immediately summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: The moment he arrived, the emperor summoned him in.

sentences.zh: 文炳拜稽首曰：「今南方已平，臣無所效力，請事北邊。」

translations.literal: Wenbing bowed prostrate and said: "Now the south is pacified; your servant has no place to exert his strength; I request to serve on the northern frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing kowtowed and said, "The south is pacified and I have no further service to offer. I beg leave to campaign on the northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕召卿，意不在是也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I summoned you, and my intent is not that.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I did not summon you for that.

sentences.zh: 豎子盜兵，朕自撫定。

translations.literal: Those petty fellows who steal armies—I shall pacify them myself.
translations.idiomatic: Petty rebels on the northern frontier—I will settle them myself.

sentences.zh: 山以南，國之根本也，盡以託卿。

translations.literal: South of the mountains is the root of the state—I entrust it all to you.
translations.idiomatic: South of the mountains lies the foundation of the realm. I entrust it all to you.

sentences.zh: 卒有不虞，便宜處置以聞。

translations.literal: If anything unexpected occurs, dispose of it at discretion and report.
translations.idiomatic: If anything unforeseen arises, handle it as you see fit and report to me.

sentences.zh: 中書省、樞密院事無大小，咨卿而行，已敕主者，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: Matters great and small of the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs—consult you before acting; I have already ordered those in charge; exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Matters great and small in the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs are to be referred to you. I have instructed the responsible officials—do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 文炳避謝，不許，因奏曰：「臣在臨安時，阿里伯奉詔檢括宋諸藏貨寶，追索沒匿甚細，人實苦之。

translations.literal: Wenbing declined and thanked him but was not permitted; he thereupon memorialized: "When your servant was at Lin'an, Alibo received orders to inventory Song's stored goods and treasures, pursuing and demanding concealed items in minute detail—the people truly suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing demurred but was overruled. He then said, "While I was at Lin'an, Alibo was ordered to inventory Song's stored goods and treasures, pursuing hidden wealth down to the smallest item. The people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 宋人未洽吾德，遽苦之以財，恐非安懷之道。」

translations.literal: The Song people have not yet been won over by our virtue; to afflict them suddenly with financial exactions— I fear this is not the way to reassure and embrace them."
translations.idiomatic: The Song people have not yet accepted our rule. To burden them with exactions now is no way to win their hearts."

sentences.zh: 即詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once canceled the order.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「昔者泉州蒲壽庚以城降，壽庚素主市舶，謂宜重其事權，使為我扞海寇，誘諸蠻臣服，因解所佩金虎符佩壽庚矣，惟陛下恕其專擅之罪。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Formerly Pu Shougen of Quanzhou surrendered the city; Shougen had long managed maritime trade—I considered it fitting to increase his authority so he could defend against sea raiders for us and induce the various barbarians to submit; I therefore removed the gold tiger tally I wore and bestowed it on Shougen—may Your Majesty pardon my unauthorized act."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "When Pu Shougen of Quanzhou surrendered, he had long managed maritime trade. I thought his authority should be strengthened so he could guard against pirates and win over the southern peoples. I gave him my own gold tiger tally—may Your Majesty forgive my presumption."

sentences.zh: 帝大嘉之，更賜金虎符。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this and bestowed another gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him highly and granted another gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 燕勞畢，即聽陛辭，文炳求見皇太子，帝許之，復敕太子曰：「董文炳所任甚重，見畢即遣行。」

translations.literal: When the feast of consolation was finished, he was immediately permitted to take leave from the steps; Wenbing asked to see the Crown Prince; the emperor granted it and again instructed the prince: "Dong Wenbing's commission is very weighty—when the audience is finished send him on his way at once."
translations.idiomatic: After the farewell banquet he was dismissed. Wenbing asked to see the Crown Prince, and the emperor agreed, instructing the prince, "Dong Wenbing's commission is weighty—send him on his way as soon as you have seen him."

sentences.zh: 既見，慰諭懇至。

translations.literal: After the audience, consolation and instruction were earnest to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The prince received him with earnest reassurance.

sentences.zh: 文炳留士選宿衛，即日就道，凡在上都三日。

translations.literal: Wenbing left Shixuan as palace guard and set out the same day; in all he was at Shangdu three days.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing left Shixuan behind as palace guard and set out the same day. His entire stay at Shangdu lasted three days.

sentences.zh: 至大都，更日至中書、樞密，不署中書案。

translations.literal: Reaching Dadu, he went daily to the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs but did not sign Secretariat documents.
translations.idiomatic: At Dadu he visited the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs daily but refused to sign Secretariat documents.

sentences.zh: 平章政事阿合馬方恃寵用事，生殺任情，惟畏文炳，奸狀為之少斂。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Ahmad was then relying on favor to wield power, killing and sparing as he pleased; he feared only Wenbing, and his wicked conduct was thereby somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Ahmad was then abusing the emperor's favor, killing and sparing at whim. He feared only Wenbing, and his misconduct was somewhat curbed.

sentences.zh: 嘗執筆請曰：「相公官為左丞，當署省案。」

translations.literal: He once took up the brush and requested: "Your Excellency's office is Left Vice Director—you ought to sign provincial documents."
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad once pressed a brush on him, saying, "As Left Vice Director you should sign the Secretariat papers."

sentences.zh: 請至再四，不肯署。

translations.literal: He requested up to four times; Wenbing refused to sign.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again and again, but Wenbing would not sign.

sentences.zh: 皇太子聞之，謂宮臣竹忽納曰：「董文炳深慮，非爾曹所知。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince heard of this and said to palace attendant Zhuhuna: "Dong Wenbing's deep considerations are not what you people understand."
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince heard of this and told his attendant Zhuhuna, "Dong Wenbing thinks far ahead—beyond what you can grasp."

sentences.zh: 後或私問其故，文炳曰：「主上所付託者，在根本之重，非文移之細。

translations.literal: Later someone privately asked the reason; Wenbing said: "What the sovereign entrusted to me lies in the weight of the foundation, not the minutiae of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone asked him privately why. Wenbing said, "The sovereign entrusted me with the weight of the foundation, not the minutiae of paperwork.

sentences.zh: 且吾少徇則濟姦，不徇則致讒。

translations.literal: Moreover, if I yield a little I aid wickedness; if I do not yield I invite slander.
translations.idiomatic: If I yield even slightly I abet wickedness; if I refuse I invite slander.

sentences.zh: 讒行則身危，而深失付託本意。

translations.literal: If slander succeeds my person is endangered, and I deeply fail the sovereign's intent in entrusting me.
translations.idiomatic: If slander succeeds I am endangered and I betray the sovereign's trust.

sentences.zh: 吾是以預其大政，而略其細務也。」

translations.literal: Therefore I participate in great policy but leave aside minor affairs."
translations.idiomatic: So I take part in great affairs of state and leave the small matters alone."

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，文炳有疾，奏請解機務，詔曰：「大都暑熾，非病者宜，卿可來此，固當愈。」

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifteenth year Wenbing fell ill and memorialized requesting to be relieved of state affairs; an edict said: "Dadu's heat is fierce—not suitable for the ill; you may come here and will surely recover."
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifteenth year (1278) Wenbing fell ill and asked to be relieved of state duties. The emperor replied, "Dadu is sweltering and ill-suited to your condition. Come north—you will recover."

sentences.zh: 文炳至上都，奏曰：「臣病不足領機務，西北高寒，筋骸舒暢，當復自愈，請盡力北邊。」

translations.literal: Wenbing reached Shangdu and memorialized: "Your servant's illness is insufficient to oversee state affairs; the northwest is high and cold, sinews and bones are at ease, and I should recover on my own—I request to exert my strength on the northern frontier."
translations.idiomatic: At Shangdu he said, "I am too ill to manage state affairs, but the cool northwest should restore me. I beg leave to serve on the northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿固忠孝，是不足行也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are indeed loyal and filial—that is not sufficient to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your loyalty and devotion are well known—that will not do.

sentences.zh: 樞密事重，以卿僉書樞密院事，中書左丞如故。」

translations.literal: Military affairs are weighty—appoint you Concurrent Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat as before."
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs are too important. You are appointed Concurrent Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs while retaining your post as Left Vice Director."

sentences.zh: 文炳辭，不許，遂拜。

translations.literal: Wenbing declined; it was not permitted; he thereupon accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing declined but was overruled and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 八月天壽節，禮成賜宴，帝命坐文炳上坐，諭宗室大臣曰：「董文炳，功臣也，理當坐是。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the Heavenly Longevity festival, when the rites were completed a feast was granted; the emperor ordered Wenbing seated in the seat of honor and instructed the imperial clansmen and great ministers: "Dong Wenbing is a meritorious minister—it is right that he sit here."
translations.idiomatic: At the Heavenly Longevity festival in the eighth month, after the rites the emperor gave a feast and seated Wenbing in the place of honor, telling the princes and ministers, "Dong Wenbing is a founding servant—he belongs in this seat."

sentences.zh: 每尚食，上食輒輟賜文炳。

translations.literal: Whenever food was served, what the emperor tasted he would set aside and bestow on Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor was served, he would set aside portions for Wenbing.

sentences.zh: 是夜，文炳疾復作，敕賜御醫日來診視。

translations.literal: That night Wenbing's illness recurred; an edict bestowed imperial physicians to come daily to examine and treat him.
translations.idiomatic: That night his illness returned. The emperor sent his own physicians to attend him daily.

sentences.zh: 九月十三日，疾篤，洗沐而坐，召文忠等曰：「吾以先人死王事，恨不為國死邊，今至此，命也。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the ninth month, critically ill, he bathed and sat upright, summoned Wenzhong and the others, and said: "Because my forebear died in the king's service, I regretted not dying for the state on the frontier; to reach this point now is fate.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the ninth month, gravely ill, he bathed, sat upright, and summoned Wenzhong and his brothers. "Our father died in the king's service. I always regretted not dying for the realm on the frontier. To come to this is fate.

sentences.zh: 願董氏世有男能騎馬者，勉力報國，則吾死瞑目矣。」

translations.literal: I wish that in every generation the Dong clan may have men who can ride horses and strive with their strength to repay the state—then I can close my eyes in death."
translations.idiomatic: May the Dong clan always produce men who can ride and serve the state with all their strength—then I can die in peace."

sentences.zh: 言畢，就枕卒。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he lay on his pillow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, he lay back on his pillow and died.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，悼痛良久，命文忠護喪葬藁城，令所過有司以禮弔祭，贈金紫光祿大夫、平章政事，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he mourned in grief for a long while, ordered Wenzhong to escort the funeral and bury him at Gaocheng, commanded the officials wherever the procession passed to offer rites of mourning and sacrifice, and posthumously granted Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp and Grand Councillor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Offering.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he mourned deeply. He ordered Wenzhong to escort the funeral to Gaocheng and commanded officials along the route to perform rites of mourning. Wenbing was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp and Grand Councillor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Offering.

sentences.zh: 子士元、士選。

translations.literal: His sons were Shiyuan and Shixuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shiyuan and Shixuan.

sentences.zh: 中統初，文蔚入典禁兵，士元以世家子選供奉內班，從車駕巡狩北方，嘗預武定山之役。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong, Wenwei entered to direct the forbidden troops; Shiyuan, as a son of an eminent house, was selected for the inner palace attendant corps, followed the imperial carriage on hunts in the north, and once took part in the campaign at Wudingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhongtong era, Wenwei took charge of the imperial guard. Shiyuan, as a son of a distinguished family, was selected for the inner palace guard, accompanied the emperor on hunts in the north, and fought at Wudingshan.

sentences.zh: 帝知其忠勤可任以事。

translations.literal: The emperor knew his loyalty and diligence and that he could be entrusted with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recognized his loyalty and diligence and judged him fit for responsible posts.

sentences.zh: 會文蔚病卒，無子，命士元襲為千夫長。

translations.literal: It happened that Wenwei died of illness without sons; Shiyuan was ordered to inherit as commander of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenwei died without heirs, Shiyuan was ordered to inherit his command as leader of a thousand.

sentences.zh: 出師南征襄、漢，分禁兵戍淮上，士元在軍中修敕武備，號令肅然。

translations.literal: When the army marched south to campaign in Xiang and Han, the forbidden troops were divided to garrison the Huai region; Shiyuan in the army rectified military equipment, and orders were sternly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign into Xiang and Han, part of the imperial guard was posted on the Huai. Shiyuan drilled the troops and restored discipline until orders rang with absolute authority.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏克江南，宋兵保兩淮未下，士元數與戰，拔淮安堡，以功遷武節將軍。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan conquered Jiangnan, Song troops held the two Huai regions and had not fallen; Shiyuan fought many times, captured Huaian Fort, and by merit was promoted to Martial Integrity General.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Bayan conquered the south, Song forces still held the two Huai regions. Shiyuan fought repeatedly, captured Huaian Fort, and was promoted to Martial Integrity General for his merit.

sentences.zh: 從太師博魯歡攻揚州，駐師灣頭堡。

translations.literal: Following Grand Preceptor Boluohan in attacking Yangzhou, the army encamped at Wantou Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Preceptor Boluohan in the attack on Yangzhou and encamped at Wantou Fort.

sentences.zh: 時方大暑，博魯歡病還京師，以行省阿里代領諸軍。

translations.literal: It was then the height of summer; Boluohan fell ill and returned to the capital; Provincial Administration Commissioner Ali took over command of the armies in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer Boluohan fell ill and returned to the capital. Provincial Commissioner Ali took command in his stead.

sentences.zh: 揚州守將姜才乘隙來攻。

translations.literal: Yangzhou's defending general Jiang Cai seized an opening to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou's defender Jiang Cai seized the moment to attack.

sentences.zh: 阿里素不習兵，率輕騎數百出堡，士元與別將哈刺禿以百騎從之。

translations.literal: Ali was by nature unskilled in warfare; he led several hundred light cavalry out of the fort; Shiyuan and Deputy Commander Halutu followed with a hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Ali had no military experience. He led several hundred light horsemen out of the fort, with Shiyuan and Deputy Commander Halutu following with a hundred cavalry.

sentences.zh: 日已暮，宋兵至者萬餘，士元謂左右曰：「大丈夫報國政在今日，勿懼也。」

translations.literal: The day had grown dark; more than ten thousand Song troops arrived. Shiyuan said to those beside him: "A great man repays the state—today is the day; do not fear."
translations.idiomatic: "A man repays his country when the moment comes—do not fear," Shiyuan told his men as more than ten thousand Song troops closed in at dusk.

sentences.zh: 方整陣欲戰，阿里趣令左旋，已乃遁去。

translations.literal: Just as he was forming ranks to fight, Ali urgently ordered a turn to the left, and then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was forming ranks to fight, Ali ordered a left wheel and fled.

sentences.zh: 士元與哈剌禿以部兵赴敵死戰，鼓譟震地，泥淖馬不能馳，乃棄馬步戰，至四更，敵衆始退。

translations.literal: Shiyuan and Halutu led their unit troops to meet the enemy and fought to the death; drums and shouts shook the earth; in the mud horses could not gallop, so they abandoned their horses and fought on foot; by the fourth watch the enemy masses at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan and Halutu led their men into a desperate fight. Drums and shouts shook the ground. Horses foundered in the mud, so they dismounted and fought on foot until the fourth watch, when the enemy finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及旦，阿里來視戰地，見士元卧泥中，身被十七槍，甲裳盡赤，肩舁至營而絕，年四十二。

translations.literal: At dawn Ali came to view the battlefield and saw Shiyuan lying in the mud, his body pierced by seventeen spears, armor and garments all red; he was carried on shoulders to camp and there expired, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Ali came to the field and found Shiyuan lying in the mud with seventeen wounds, his armor soaked red. He was carried to camp and died there, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 哈剌禿亦戰死。

translations.literal: Halutu also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Halutu also fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 江淮既平，伯顏入朝言於帝曰：「淮海之役，所損者二將而已。」

translations.literal: When the Jiang and Huai regions were pacified, Bayan entered court and said to the emperor: "In the Huai-Hai campaign, the loss was only two generals."
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiang-Huai region was pacified, Bayan reported to court: "In the Huai-Hai campaign we lost only two generals."

sentences.zh: 帝問其人，以士元與哈剌禿對。

translations.literal: The emperor asked who they were; he answered with Shiyuan and Halutu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked their names and was told Shiyuan and Halutu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不花健捷過人，晝戰必能制敵，夜戰而死，甚可惜也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Buhua was vigorous and swift beyond others; in daylight battle he was sure to overcome the enemy—to die in night fighting is deeply regrettable."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Buhua was exceptionally bold and swift—by day he always mastered the enemy. To die in a night battle is a great pity."

sentences.zh: 至大元年，贈鎮國上將軍、僉書樞密院事，諡節愍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was posthumously granted Defender-General of the State and Concurrent Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with the posthumous title Temperate and Lamented.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was posthumously made Defender-General of the State and Concurrent Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with the posthumous title Temperate and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 後加贈推誠效節功臣、資德大夫、中書左丞、護軍，追封趙郡公，改諡忠愍。

translations.literal: Later he received additional posthumous honors as Meritorious Minister of Sincere Loyalty and Exemplary Integrity, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Guardian of the Army; was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao commandery posthumously, and his posthumous title was changed to Loyal and Lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Later honors were added: Meritorious Minister of Sincere Loyalty, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, Left Vice Director, Guardian of the Army, and posthumous Duke of Zhao, with the title changed to Loyal and Lamented.

sentences.zh: 士選字舜卿，文炳次子也。

translations.literal: Shixuan, courtesy name Shunqing, was Wenbing's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan, courtesy name Shunqing, was Wenbing's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼從文炳居兵間，晝治武事，夜讀書不輟。

translations.literal: From childhood he followed Wenbing amid armies; by day he trained in military affairs, by night he read books without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he followed his father on campaign, drilling by day and reading books at night without pause.

sentences.zh: 文炳緫師與宋兵戰金山，士選戰甚力，大敗之，追至海而還。

translations.literal: When Wenbing commanded the army in battle with Song troops at Jinshan, Shixuan fought with great force, routed them greatly, pursued to the sea and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbing fought Song forces at Jinshan, Shixuan fought fiercely, routed them, and pursued to the coast before turning back.

sentences.zh: 及降張瑄等，丞相伯顏臨陣觀之，壯其驍勇，遣使問之，始知為文炳子。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xuan and others surrendered, Chancellor Bayan observed the battle and admired his valor and daring; he sent to ask who he was and only then learned he was Wenbing's son.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xuan surrendered, Bayan watched the fighting and admired his courage, then learned he was Wenbing's son.

sentences.zh: 奏功，佩金符，為管軍緫管。

translations.literal: His merit was memorialized; he was granted a gold tally and appointed Commander-in-Chief of army management.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds were reported; he received a gold tally and was made Commander-in-Chief of army management.

sentences.zh: 戰數有功。

translations.literal: In battle he achieved merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in battle again and again.

sentences.zh: 宋降，從文炳入宋宮，取宋主降表及收其文書圖籍，靜重識大體，秋毫無所取，軍中稱之。

translations.literal: When Song surrendered, he followed Wenbing into the Song palace, took the Song ruler's surrender document and collected documents and records; he was calm and weighty and understood the larger pattern, taking not the slightest thing, and the army praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Song surrendered he entered the palace with Wenbing, took the surrender document and archives, and touched nothing—calm, dignified, and principled, as the army acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 宋平，班師，詔置侍衛親軍諸衛，以士選為前衛指揮使，號令明正，得士大夫心。

translations.literal: When Song was pacified the army withdrew; an edict established the various guards of the personal guard army; Shixuan was made Commander of the Forward Guard; his orders were clear and correct, and he won the hearts of scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification he was made Commander of the Forward Guard with clear and upright orders that won scholar-officials' respect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以其職讓其弟士秀。

translations.literal: Before long he yielded this post to his younger brother Shixiu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he yielded the post to his younger brother Shixiu.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his generosity.

sentences.zh: 命士秀將前衛，而以士選同僉行樞密院事於湖廣，久之召還。

translations.literal: He ordered Shixiu to command the Forward Guard, while Shixuan was made Concurrent Secretary conducting Bureau affairs in Huguang; after a long time he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu took the Forward Guard; Shixuan served concurrently in Huguang and was later recalled.

sentences.zh: 宗王乃顏叛，帝親征，召士選至行在所，與李勞山同將漢人諸軍以禦之。

translations.literal: The imperial prince Nayan rebelled; the emperor campaigned in person and summoned Shixuan to the mobile court; he and Li Laoshan together commanded the various Han armies to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Nayan rebelled, the emperor summoned Shixuan to campaign with Li Laoshan commanding Han forces.

sentences.zh: 乃顏軍飛矢及乘輿前，士選等出步卒橫擊之，其衆敗走。

translations.literal: Nayan's army's flying arrows reached before the imperial carriage; Shixuan and the others sent out foot soldiers in a lateral strike; their masses were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When arrows reached the imperial carriage, Shixuan sent infantry in a flanking attack and routed Nayan's troops.

sentences.zh: 緩急進退有禮，帝甚善之。

translations.literal: In urgency and ease, advance and retreat, he observed propriety; the emperor greatly approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: In advance and retreat he observed propriety, and the emperor greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 桑哥事敗，帝求直士用之，以易其弊，於是召士選論議政事，以中書左丞與平章政事徹理往鎮浙西，聽辟舉僚屬。

translations.literal: When Sangge's affair failed, the emperor sought upright men to use them to remedy abuses; he thereupon summoned Shixuan to discuss government affairs, and appointed him Left Vice Director of the Secretariat to go with Grand Councillor Cheli to pacify western Zhe, with authority to recruit staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangge's fall the emperor sought upright men; Shixuan was made Left Vice Director and sent with Cheli to western Zhe with power to recruit staff.

sentences.zh: 至部，察病民事，悉以帝意除之，民大悅。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he investigated matters harming the people and removed them all according to the emperor's intent; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he investigated abuses harming the people and removed them by imperial intent; the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 有聚斂之臣為奸利，事發得罪且死，詐言所遣舶商海外未至，請留以待之，士選曰：「海商至則捕錄之，不至則無如之何，不係斯人之存亡也。

translations.literal: A minister who gathered wealth for illicit profit, when his affair was exposed, was guilty and faced death; he falsely claimed the merchant ships he had sent overseas had not yet returned and asked to be kept waiting; Shixuan said: "When the overseas merchants arrive they can be arrested and recorded; if they do not arrive, nothing can be done—it does not depend on this man's life or death.
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt official facing death claimed his merchant ships had not returned. Shixuan said, "If they arrive, arrest them; if not, this man's life is irrelevant.

sentences.zh: 苟此人幸存，則無以謝天下。」

translations.literal: If this man survives, there is no way to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: If he survives, how can we answer to the realm?"

sentences.zh: 遂竟其罪。

translations.literal: His crime was thereupon carried through.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was carried out.
