sentences.zh: 浙多湖泊，廣蓄泄以藝水旱，率為豪民占以種藝，水無所居積，故數有水旱，士選與徹理力開復之。

translations.literal: Zhe has many lakes; broad storage and drainage for flood and drought were mostly occupied by powerful families for planting; water had nowhere to settle, hence frequent floods and droughts; Shixuan and Cheli strove to reopen and restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe's lakes, seized by powerful families, caused floods and droughts; Shixuan and Cheli restored them.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，僉行樞密院於建康。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, he was made Concurrent Secretary of the Bureau at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzong he served concurrently at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜江西行省左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Left Vice Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 贛州盜劉六十偽立名號，聚衆至萬餘。

translations.literal: In Ganzhou the bandit Liu Liushi falsely established a title and gathered more than ten thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: At Ganzhou the bandit Liu Liushi raised a title and gathered ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣兵討之，主將觀望退縮不肯戰，守吏又因以擾良民，賊勢益盛。

translations.literal: The court sent troops to suppress them; the commander-in-chief watched and shrank back, unwilling to fight; local officials also used the occasion to harass good people; the bandit force grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops hung back while officials harassed the people, and the rebels grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 士選請自往，衆欣然託之。

translations.literal: Shixuan requested to go in person; the multitude gladly entrusted itself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan volunteered; all gladly entrusted themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 即日就道，不求益兵，但率掾史李霆鎮、元明善二人，持文書以去，衆莫測其所為。

translations.literal: That same day he set out, not seeking additional troops, but leading only clerks Li Tingzhen and Yuan Mingshan, carrying documents as he went; none could fathom his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He left the same day with only two clerks and documents, to everyone's puzzlement.

sentences.zh: 至贛境，捕官吏害民者治之，民相告語曰：「不知有官法如此。」

translations.literal: Reaching Gan territory he arrested officials who harmed the people and punished them; the people told one another: "We did not know official law could be like this."
translations.idiomatic: In Gan he punished harmful officials; the people marveled at such justice.

sentences.zh: 進至興國縣，去賊巢不百里，命擇將校分兵守地待命。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xingguo county, less than a hundred li from the bandit nest, he ordered chosen commanders to divide troops, guard the ground, and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Near the rebel nest he divided troops and waited.

sentences.zh: 察知激亂之人，悉置于法，復誅奸民之為囊橐者。

translations.literal: Those he found had incited disorder were all dealt with by law; he also executed wicked people who served as their storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: He punished inciters and accomplices by law.

sentences.zh: 於是民爭出請自效，不數日遂擒賊魁，散餘衆歸農。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people competed to come forward offering to serve; within a few days the bandit chieftain was captured and the remainder dispersed to farming.
translations.idiomatic: The people rallied; within days the chief was captured and the rest sent to farm.

sentences.zh: 軍中獲賊所為文書，旁近郡縣富人姓名具在。

translations.literal: In the army documents seized from the bandits listed wealthy households of neighboring prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Captured documents listed wealthy households in nearby counties.

sentences.zh: 霆鎮、明善請焚之，民心益安。

translations.literal: Tingzhen and Mingshan asked to burn them; popular hearts were thereby more at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His clerks asked to burn them, easing popular hearts.

sentences.zh: 遣使以事平報于朝。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to report the affair pacified to court.
translations.idiomatic: He reported pacification to court.

sentences.zh: 中書平章政事不忽木召其使謂之曰：「董公上功簿邪？」

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Bukha summoned the messenger and said to him: "Has Director Dong submitted a merit register?"
translations.idiomatic: Bukha asked the messenger, "Has Director Dong submitted a merit register?"

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「某且行，左丞授之言曰：『朝廷若以軍功為問，但言鎮撫無狀，得免罪幸甚，何功之可言！』」

translations.literal: The messenger said: "I am about to depart; the Vice Director instructed me to say: 'If the court asks about military merit, only say that because pacification was inadequate I am fortunate to escape guilt—what merit can be spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: The messenger said, "The Vice Director told me: if asked about merit, say only that I am lucky to escape blame for inadequate pacification—what merit is there?

sentences.zh: 因出其書，但請黜贓吏數人而已，不言破賊事。

translations.literal: He thereupon produced his document, only requesting dismissal of several corrupt officials, not speaking of defeating bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: His memorial only asked to dismiss corrupt officials, not mentioning defeating bandits."

sentences.zh: 廷議深歎其知體而不伐。

translations.literal: Court discussion deeply admired his understanding of propriety and not boasting.
translations.idiomatic: The court admired his propriety and lack of boasting.

sentences.zh: 拜江南行御史臺中丞，廉威素著，不嚴而肅，凜然有大臣風。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate; his integrity and authority had long been established; without severity there was respect; he was stern as a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Censor-in-Chief of Jiangnan, stern and respected without harshness.

sentences.zh: 入僉樞密院事，俄拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered to serve concurrently in the Bureau of Military Affairs; soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Bureau and soon became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 前中丞崔彧久任風紀，善斡旋以就事功。

translations.literal: The former Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu had long held discipline and was skilled at maneuvering to accomplish tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Former Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu had long held discipline and maneuvered ably.

sentences.zh: 既卒，不忽木以平章軍國重事繼之，方正持大體，天下望之，而已多病，遂以屬之士選。

translations.literal: After he died, Bukha succeeded him as Grand Councillor of important state affairs, upright and holding the larger pattern—the realm looked to him—but he was already often ill, and the post was therefore entrusted to Shixuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu died, Bukha succeeded but fell ill; the post went to Shixuan.

sentences.zh: 風采明俊，中外竦然。

translations.literal: His bearing was bright and distinguished; within and without he was revered.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was distinguished; all revered him.

sentences.zh: 時丞相完澤用劉深言，出師征八百媳婦國，遠冒煙瘴，及至未戰，士卒死者十已七八。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Councillor Wanze, using Liu Shen's advice, campaigned against the Eight Hundred Wives kingdom, braving miasma far away; when they arrived they had not yet fought, and seven or eight tenths of the soldiers were already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Wanze, following Liu Shen, campaigned against the Eight Hundred Wives kingdom; before battle seven or eight tenths of the troops died of miasma.

sentences.zh: 驅民轉粟餉軍，谿谷之間不容舟車，必負擔以達。

translations.literal: The people were driven to transport grain to supply the army; between streams and valleys boats and carts could not pass, and they had to carry on shoulders to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: People carried grain on their backs where boats and carts could not pass.

sentences.zh: 一夫致粟八斗，率數人佐之，凡數十日乃至。

translations.literal: One man delivered eight dou of grain, generally several men assisting; in all it took several tens of days to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: One man carried eight dou, aided by several others, for weeks on end.

sentences.zh: 由是民死者亦數十萬，中外騷然。

translations.literal: Because of this the people who died also numbered in the hundreds of thousands; within and without there was turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of thousands of civilians died; the realm was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 而完澤說帝：「江南之地盡世祖所取，陛下不興此役，則無功可見於後世。」

translations.literal: Yet Wanze persuaded the emperor: "The lands of Jiangnan were all taken by Shizu; if Your Majesty does not undertake this campaign, there will be no achievement visible to later generations."
translations.idiomatic: Wanze told the emperor, "Jiangnan was won by Kublai—without this campaign you will leave no achievement to posterity."

sentences.zh: 帝入其言，用兵意甚堅，故無敢諫者。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words; his intent to use troops was very firm, so none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this; his resolve was firm and none dared remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 士選率同列言之，奏事殿中畢，同列皆起，士選乃獨言：「今劉深出師，以有用之民而取無用之地。

translations.literal: Shixuan led his colleagues in speaking; when memorial business in the hall was finished, his colleagues all rose; Shixuan alone spoke: "Now Liu Shen campaigns; he uses useful people to take useless land.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan alone remained and said, "Liu Shen uses useful people to take useless land.

sentences.zh: 就令當取，亦必遣使諭之，諭之不從，然後聚糧選兵，視時而動。

translations.literal: Even if it should be taken, envoys must first be sent to instruct them; if they do not obey, then gather grain, select troops, and act according to the time.
translations.idiomatic: Even if it must be taken, send envoys first; only if they refuse, gather grain and troops and act in season.

sentences.zh: 豈得輕用一人妄言，而致百萬生靈於死地？」

translations.literal: How can one lightly use one man's reckless words and consign a million living souls to the land of death?
translations.idiomatic: How can one man's reckless words consign a million souls to death?"

sentences.zh: 帝色變，士選猶明辨不止，侍從皆為之戰慄，帝曰：「事已成，卿勿復言。」

translations.literal: The emperor's countenance changed; Shixuan still argued clearly without stopping; attendants all trembled for him; the emperor said: "The affair is already done—you need not speak further."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed; attendants trembled; the emperor said, "It is settled—speak no more."

sentences.zh: 士選曰：「以言受罪，臣之所當。

translations.literal: Shixuan said: "To suffer punishment for speaking is what your servant should accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shixuan said, "Punishment for speaking is what I accept.

sentences.zh: 他日以不言罪臣，臣死何益！」

translations.literal: Later if I am punished for not speaking, what good is my death to the state!
translations.idiomatic: But if later I am punished for silence, what good is my death?"

sentences.zh: 帝麾之起，左右擁之以出。

translations.literal: The emperor waved him to rise; attendants on both sides supported him as he went out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waved him out; attendants escorted him.

sentences.zh: 未數月，帝聞師敗績，慨然曰：「董二哥之言驗矣，吾愧之。」

translations.literal: Within a few months the emperor heard the army had been defeated and sighed: "Second Brother Dong's words have been verified—I am ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: Months later, hearing of defeat, the emperor sighed, "Second Brother Dong was right—I am ashamed."

sentences.zh: 因賜上尊以旌直言，始為罷兵，誅劉深等。

translations.literal: He thereupon bestowed fine wine to honor forthright speech, and for the first time halted the troops and executed Liu Shen and others.
translations.idiomatic: He honored forthright speech with fine wine, halted the troops, and executed Liu Shen.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗呼文炳曰董大哥，故帝以二哥呼士選。

translations.literal: Shizu had called Wenbing Elder Brother Dong, so the emperor called Shixuan Second Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had called Wenbing Elder Brother Dong; hence the emperor called Shixuan Second Brother.

sentences.zh: 久之出為江浙行省右丞，遷汴梁行省平章政事，又遷陝西。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as Right Vice Director of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat, was transferred to Grand Councillor of the Bianliang Branch Secretariat, and again transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in Zhejiang, Bianliang, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 士選平生以忠義自許，尤號廉介，自門生部曲，無敢持一毫獻者。

translations.literal: Shixuan throughout his life took loyalty and righteousness as his pledge, especially known for integrity; from his students and household troops, none dared present even a single hair.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged loyalty and righteousness and was famed for integrity; none dared offer him the slightest gift.

sentences.zh: 治家甚嚴，而孝弟尤篤。

translations.literal: He managed the household very strictly, yet filial piety and brotherly duty were especially earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He ran his household strictly with deep filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 時言世家有禮法者，必歸之董氏。

translations.literal: At the time those who spoke of eminent houses with ritual propriety were sure to point to the Dong clan.
translations.idiomatic: Eminent houses with ritual propriety were said to be the Dong clan.

sentences.zh: 其禮敬賢士尤至。

translations.literal: His ritual respect for worthy scholars was especially thorough.
translations.idiomatic: He especially honored worthy scholars.

sentences.zh: 在江西，以屬掾元明善為賓友，既又得吳澄而師之，延虞汲於家塾以教其子。

translations.literal: In Jiangxi he took subordinate Yuan Mingshan as guest-friend; he also obtained Wu Cheng and took him as teacher; he extended Yan Ji in the family school to teach his sons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he befriended Yuan Mingshan, studied with Wu Cheng, and had Yan Ji teach his sons.

sentences.zh: 諸老儒及西蜀遺士，皆以書院之祿起之。

translations.literal: Old Confucian scholars and surviving scholars of western Shu were all raised on academy stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Old scholars of Shu were supported on academy stipends.

sentences.zh: 使以所學教授。

translations.literal: He had them teach with what they had learned.
translations.idiomatic: He had them teach their learning.

sentences.zh: 遷南行臺，又招汲子集與俱，後又得范等數人。

translations.literal: Transferring to the Southern Censorate, he also recruited Ji's son Ji to accompany him; later he also obtained Fan Lin and several others.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Censorate he recruited Yan Ji's son and Fan Lin.

sentences.zh: 皆以文學大顯於時。

translations.literal: All became greatly renowned in letters at the time.
translations.idiomatic: All achieved literary renown.

sentences.zh: 故世稱求賢薦士，亦必以董氏為首。

translations.literal: Therefore the age said that in seeking worthies and recommending scholars, the Dong clan was always foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking worthies and recommending scholars, the Dong clan was always named first.

sentences.zh: 晚年好讀易，澹然終其身。

translations.literal: In his later years he loved reading the Changes and lived plainly to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he loved the Changes and lived plainly to the end.

sentences.zh: 每一之官，必賣先業田廬為行貲，故老而益貧，子孫不異布衣之士，仕者往往稱廉吏云。

translations.literal: Whenever he took up an office he would sell his family's former fields and houses for travel expenses, so in old age he grew poorer; his descendants were no different from commoners; those who served office were often called incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: Each new post he sold family land for travel expenses, grew poorer in old age, and his descendants lived like commoners—many became known as honest officials.

sentences.zh: 子守忠，雲南行省參知政事；

translations.literal: His son Shouzhong was Vice Director of the Secretariat of the Yunnan Branch;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouzhong was Vice Director of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 守慤，侍正府判官；

translations.literal: Shouque was judge of the Attendant-Properness Office;
translations.idiomatic: Shouque was judge of the Attendant-Properness Office;

sentences.zh: 守思，知威州。

translations.literal: Shousi was magistrate of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shousi was magistrate of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 張弘範

translations.literal: Zhang Hongfan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongfan

sentences.zh: 張弘範字仲疇，柔第九子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongfan, courtesy name Zhongchou, was the ninth son of Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongfan, courtesy name Zhongchou, was Rou's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 善馬槊，頗能為歌詩。

translations.literal: He was skilled with the horse lance and could compose songs and poems.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled with the horse lance and could write songs and poems.

sentences.zh: 年二十時，兄順天路緫管弘略上計壽陽行都，留弘範攝府事，吏民服其明決。

translations.literal: At age twenty, when his elder brother Honglue, Route Commander of Shuntian, went up to account at the mobile capital at Shouyang, he left Hongfan to act as prefect; clerks and people submitted to his clear decisions.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty, when his brother Honglue went to account at Shouyang, Hongfan acted as prefect and won respect for clear decisions.

sentences.zh: 蒙古軍所過肆暴，弘範杖遣之，入其境無敢犯者。

translations.literal: Wherever Mongol armies passed they committed violence; Hongfan beat and sent them away; within his jurisdiction none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol troops plundered wherever they passed; Hongfan beat and expelled them, and none dared offend his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 中統初，授御用局緫管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong he was appointed Director-General of the Imperial Use Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhongtong he was appointed Director-General of the Imperial Use Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三年，改行軍緫管，從親王合必赤討李璮於濟南。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Campaign Commander-in-Chief and followed Prince Hebichi in attacking Li Tan at Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Campaign Commander-in-Chief and followed Prince Hebichi against Li Tan at Jinan.

sentences.zh: 柔戒之曰：「汝圍城勿避險地。

translations.literal: Rou admonished him: "When you besiege a city do not avoid dangerous ground.
translations.idiomatic: Rou warned him, "When besieging a city do not avoid dangerous ground.

sentences.zh: 汝無怠心，則兵必致死。

translations.literal: If you have no slack mind, the troops are sure to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: If you never slacken, your men will fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 主者慮其險。

translations.literal: The commander worries about the danger.
translations.idiomatic: The commander fears the danger.

sentences.zh: 苟有來犯，必赴救，可因以立功，勉之。」

translations.literal: If there is an attack, he is sure to come to the rescue; you can thereby achieve merit—exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: If attacked, he must rescue you—you can win merit thereby. Exert yourself."

sentences.zh: 弘範營城西，璮出軍突諸將營，獨不向弘範。

translations.literal: Hongfan encamped west of the city; Tan sent troops in a sudden strike at the various generals' camps, alone not toward Hongfan.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan encamped west of the city. Tan struck the other generals' camps but not Hongfan's.

sentences.zh: 弘範曰：「我營險地，璮乃示弱於我，必以奇兵來襲，謂我弗悟也。」

translations.literal: Hongfan said: "My camp is in dangerous ground; Tan is showing weakness toward me—he is sure to come with strange troops in a surprise attack, thinking I do not understand."
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan said, "My camp is in dangerous ground—Tan is feigning weakness and will raid me by surprise."

sentences.zh: 遂築長壘，內伏甲士，而外為壕，開東門以待之，夜令士卒浚濠益深廣，璮不知也。

translations.literal: He thereupon built a long rampart, with armored soldiers hidden within and an outer moat; he opened the east gate to await them; at night he ordered soldiers to deepen and widen the moat—Tan did not know.
translations.idiomatic: He built a long rampart with hidden soldiers and a moat, opened the east gate as bait, and deepened the moat by night unbeknown to Tan.

sentences.zh: 明日，果擁飛橋來攻，未及岸，軍陷壕中，得跨壕而上者，突入壘門，遇伏皆死，降兩賊將。

translations.literal: The next day they indeed brought flying bridges to attack; before reaching the bank the army fell into the moat; those who could cross the moat and mount entered the rampart gate; meeting the ambush all died; two bandit generals surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they attacked with flying bridges; men fell into the moat; those who crossed met the ambush and died; two rebel generals surrendered.

sentences.zh: 柔聞之曰：「真吾子也。」

translations.literal: Rou heard and said: "Truly my son."
translations.idiomatic: Rou heard and said, "Truly my son."

sentences.zh: 璮既誅，朝廷懲璮盡專兵民之權，故能為亂，議罷大藩子弟之在官者，弘範例罷。

translations.literal: After Tan was executed, the court, chastened by how he had monopolized control over both troops and civilians and thus been able to rebel, deliberated removing from office the sons and younger brothers of great feudatories, and Hongfan was dismissed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Tan was put to death, the court blamed his rebellion on his monopoly of military and civil authority and proposed removing great feudatories' sons from office; Hongfan was dismissed under the same rule.

sentences.zh: 六年，括諸道兵圍宋襄陽，授益都淄萊等路行軍萬戶，復佩金虎符。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, troops from all circuits were conscripted to besiege Song Xiangyang; he was appointed Mobile Corps Ten-thousand Household of the Yidu, Zilai, and other routes, and again wore the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, conscripts from every circuit besieged Song Xiangyang; Hongfan was made Mobile Corps commander of the Yidu-Zilai routes and again given the golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以益都兵乃李璮所教練之卒，勇悍難制，故命領之。

translations.literal: The court, because the Yidu troops were soldiers trained by Li Tan, fierce and hard to control, therefore ordered him to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Yidu force was Li Tan's old training cadre—fierce and unruly—the court put Hongfan in charge of them.

sentences.zh: 戍鹿門堡，以斷宋餉道，且絕郢之救兵。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Lumen Fort to cut the Song supply route and also to block relief troops from Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He held Lumen Fort to sever Song supply lines and block relief from Ying.

sentences.zh: 弘範建言曰：「國家取襄陽，為延久之計者，所以重人命而欲其自斃也。

translations.literal: Hongfan submitted advice, saying: 'The state is taking Xiangyang by a prolonged plan in order to value human lives and wish that it destroy itself.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan argued that the long siege of Xiangyang was meant to spare lives and let the city collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 曩者，夏貴乘江漲送衣糧入城，我師坐視，無禦之者。

translations.literal: Formerly, Xia Gui, riding the river's rise, sent clothing and grain into the city; our army sat and watched, with none to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xia Gui had used flood season to slip supplies into the city while our forces looked on without interference.

sentences.zh: 而其境南接江陵、歸、峽，商販行旅士卒絡繹不絕，寧有自斃之時乎！

translations.literal: Yet on its south it connects with Jiangling, Gui, and Xia; merchants, travelers, and soldiers come and go without end—how could there be a time of self-destruction!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the south still fed Xiangyang through Jiangling, Gui, and Xia—how could it ever collapse if trade and reinforcements never stopped?

sentences.zh: 宜城萬山以斷其西，柵灌子灘以絕其東，則庶幾速斃之道也。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to fortify Wanshan to cut it on the west and palisade Guanzi Bay to sever it on the east; then perhaps there will be a way of quick destruction.'
translations.idiomatic: We should fortify Wanshan in the west and block Guanzi Bay in the east—that is the way to bring the city down quickly.

sentences.zh: 帥府奏用其言，移弘範兵千人戍萬山。

translations.literal: The command headquarters submitted his words for adoption and moved a thousand of Hongfan's troops to garrison Wanshan.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters adopted his plan and posted a thousand of Hongfan's men at Wanshan.

sentences.zh: 既城，與將士較射出東門，宋師奄至。

translations.literal: After the fort was built, he went out the east gate with officers and soldiers for an archery match, and Song forces suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fort was finished, he took his men out the east gate for archery practice when Song troops suddenly appeared.

sentences.zh: 將佐皆謂衆寡不敵，宜入城自守。

translations.literal: The generals and aides all said the many were too few to match and that they ought to enter the city and defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: His officers argued they were outnumbered and should retreat behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 弘範曰：「吾與諸君在此何事，敵至將不戰乎？

translations.literal: Hongfan said: 'For what purpose are I and you gentlemen here? When the enemy comes, will we not fight?
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan said, 'Why else are we here? When the enemy comes, will we refuse to fight?

sentences.zh: 敢言退者死。」

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak of retreat shall die.'
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who talks of retreat will die.'

sentences.zh: 即擐甲上馬，立遣偏將李庭當其前，他將攻其後，親率二百騎為長陣，令曰：「聞吾鼓則進，未鼓勿動。」

translations.literal: At once he donned armor and mounted, immediately sent the lieutenant general Li Ting to meet them in front, other generals to attack from behind, and personally led two hundred horsemen in a long formation, giving the order: 'When you hear my drum, advance; before the drum, do not move.'
translations.idiomatic: He armored, mounted, sent Li Ting to the front and other commanders to the rear, and personally led two hundred cavalry in line, ordering, 'Advance at my drum; until then, hold your ground.'

sentences.zh: 宋軍步騎相間突陣，弘範軍不動，再進再却，弘範曰：「彼氣衰矣。」

translations.literal: Song infantry and cavalry alternately burst against the formation; Hongfan's army did not move; they advanced again and retreated again; Hongfan said: 'Their fighting spirit is waning.'
translations.idiomatic: Song infantry and cavalry charged in waves, but Hongfan's men held; after two feints Hongfan said, 'Their spirit is broken.'

sentences.zh: 鼓之，前後奮擊，宋師奔潰。

translations.literal: He beat the drum; front and rear struck with vigor, and the Song army fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: He sounded the drum; his forces struck from front and rear, and the Song army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 八年，築一字城逼襄陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, a single-line wall-city was built to press upon Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, he built a linked-wall siege line to tighten the noose on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 破樊城外郭。

translations.literal: The outer wall of Fancheng was broken.
translations.idiomatic: The outer defenses of Fancheng were breached.

sentences.zh: 九年，攻樊城，流矢中其肘，裹瘡見主帥曰：「襄、樊相為唇齒，故不可破。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, attacking Fancheng, a stray arrow struck his elbow; he bound the wound and went to see the supreme commander, saying: 'Xiang and Fan are lip and teeth to each other, and therefore cannot be broken.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, while assaulting Fancheng, he was struck in the elbow; bandaged, he told the commander, 'Xiangyang and Fancheng stand or fall together—you cannot take one alone.

sentences.zh: 若截江道，斷其援兵，水陸夾攻，樊必破矣。

translations.literal: If the river route is cut off and relief troops blocked, with land and water attack together, Fan will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Cut the river and block reinforcements, then press from land and water—Fancheng will fall.

sentences.zh: 樊破則襄陽何所恃。」

translations.literal: If Fan is broken, what will Xiangyang rely upon?'
translations.idiomatic: Once Fancheng falls, what can Xiangyang depend on?'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His advice was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The commander agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，復出銳卒先登，遂拔之。

translations.literal: The next day, he again sent elite troops to lead the ascent and thus captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent elite troops up first and took the city.

sentences.zh: 襄陽既下，偕宋將呂文煥入覲，賜錦衣、白金、寶鞍，將校行賞有差。

translations.literal: Once Xiangyang had fallen, together with the Song general Lü Wenhuan he entered audience; brocade robes, white gold, and a precious saddle were bestowed, and officers and commanders received rewards in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangyang fell, he and the Song commander Lü Wenhuan were received in audience and rewarded with brocade, silver, and a fine saddle; ranks below were also rewarded.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丞相伯顏伐宋，弘範率左部諸軍循漢江，東略郢西，南攻武磯堡，取之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Chancellor Bayan attacked Song; Hongfan led the left-section armies along the Han River, raided eastward in the region west of Ying, attacked south at Wuji Fort, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, when Chancellor Bayan invaded Song, Hongfan led the left wing down the Han, swept the west of Ying, and captured Wuji Fort.

sentences.zh: 北兵渡江，弘範為前鋒。

translations.literal: When the northern army crossed the river, Hongfan served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan army crossed the Yangzi, Hongfan led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 宋相賈似道督兵阻蕪湖，殿帥孫虎臣據丁家洲。

translations.literal: Song Chancellor Jia Sidao supervised troops to block at Wuhu; the Rear Guard Marshal Sun Huchen held Dingjiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chancellor Jia Sidao mustered troops at Wuhu while Rear Guard Marshal Sun Huchen held Dingjiazhou.

sentences.zh: 弘範轉戰而前，諸軍繼之，宋師潰，弘範長驅至建康。

translations.literal: Hongfan fought his way forward; the armies followed; the Song army was routed; Hongfan drove straight through to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan fought forward while the main force followed; the Song line collapsed, and he raced on to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月，帝遣使諭丞相毋輕敵貪進，方暑，其少駐以待。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year, the emperor sent a messenger instructing the chancellor not to treat the enemy lightly and be greedy for advance; it was just summer heat—he should halt awhile and wait.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year twelve, the emperor sent word telling Bayan not to underestimate the enemy or push too hard in the summer heat, but to pause and wait.

sentences.zh: 弘範進曰：「聖恩待士卒誠厚，然緩急之宜，非可遙度。

translations.literal: Hongfan advanced and said: 'Imperial grace toward the soldiers is truly generous, yet what is fitting in urgency or ease cannot be measured from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan replied that the emperor's care for the troops was generous, but commanders on the spot alone could judge pace.

sentences.zh: 今敵已奪氣，正當乘破竹之勢，取之無遺策矣。

translations.literal: Now the enemy's spirit is already seized; it is exactly the time to ride the momentum of splitting bamboo—there will be no strategy left untaken.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's spirit is broken; now is the moment to press like bamboo splitting—no better opening will come.

sentences.zh: 豈宜迂緩，使敵得為計耶？」

translations.literal: How can one be dilatory and roundabout, letting the enemy devise plans?'
translations.idiomatic: Why delay and give the enemy time to recover?

sentences.zh: 丞相然之，馳驛至闕，面論形勢，得旨進師。

translations.literal: The chancellor assented, raced by post relay to the palace, argued the situation face to face, and received the edict to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan agreed, rode posthaste to court, argued the case in person, and won permission to march on.

sentences.zh: 十二年，次瓜洲，分兵立柵，據其要害，揚州都統姜才所統兵勁悍善戰，至是以二萬人出揚子橋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, encamped at Guazhou, he divided troops to erect palisades and hold the vital points; the troops commanded by Yangzhou Commander-in-Chief Jiang Cai were fierce and skilled in battle, and on this occasion came out with twenty thousand men at Yangzi Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he halted at Guazhou, posted troops at key points, and faced Jiang Cai of Yangzhou—a fierce commander—who marched twenty thousand men out to Yangzi Bridge.

sentences.zh: 弘範佐都元帥阿朮禦之，與宋兵夾水陣。

translations.literal: Hongfan assisted the Grand Marshal Aju in resisting them, and formed battle lines facing the Song army across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan assisted Grand Marshal Aju, drawing up battle lines across the water from the Song force.

sentences.zh: 弘範以十三騎徑度衝之，陣堅不動，弘範引却。

translations.literal: Hongfan with thirteen horsemen crossed directly and charged; the formation stood firm without moving; Hongfan drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan charged across with thirteen riders, but the Song line held firm, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 一騎躍馬揮刀，直趣弘範，弘範旋轡反迎刺之，應手頓斃馬下，其衆潰亂，追至城門，斬首萬餘級，自相蹂藉溺死者過半。

translations.literal: One rider leaped his horse and swung his blade, charging straight at Hongfan; Hongfan wheeled his bridle and turned to meet and stab him; at the touch of his hand the man instantly fell dead beneath his horse; their masses broke in disorder; pursuing to the city gate, more than ten thousand heads were cut off, and over half died by trampling one another or drowning.
translations.idiomatic: One rider broke ranks and charged Hongfan; Hongfan wheeled and ran him through, and at once the man fell dead; the Song force collapsed, and in the pursuit to the city gate more than ten thousand were killed—over half trampled or drowned.

sentences.zh: 宋將張世傑、孫虎臣等率水軍於焦山決戰，弘範以一軍從旁橫衝之，宋師遂敗。

translations.literal: Song generals Zhang Shijie, Sun Huchen, and others led the navy in decisive battle at Jiaoshan; Hongfan took one army and struck across from the flank; the Song army was thus defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen brought the Song fleet to battle at Jiaoshan; Hongfan hit them from the flank with a separate force, and the Song navy was broken.

sentences.zh: 追至圌山之東，奪戰艦八十艘，俘馘千數。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the east of Tu Mountain, eighty warships were seized and captives and severed heads numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached the east of Mount Tu, where they captured eighty warships and took thousands of prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 上其功，改亳州萬戶，後賜名拔都。

translations.literal: He submitted his achievement; he was changed to Ten-thousand Household of Bozhou; later he was granted the name Batu.
translations.idiomatic: He reported his victories, was made commander of Bozhou, and later received the honorific name Batu.

sentences.zh: 從中書左丞董文炳，由海道會丞相伯顏，進次近郊。

translations.literal: Following Left Assistant Grand Councillor of the Secretariat Dong Wenbing, by the sea route he joined Chancellor Bayan and advanced to encamp in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Left Councillor Dong Wenbing by sea, met Bayan, and marched to the outskirts of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宋主上降表，以伯姪為稱，往返未決。

translations.literal: The Song ruler sent up a surrender memorial, using uncle-and-nephew as the form of address; going back and forth, no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor offered surrender on uncle-nephew terms, but negotiations dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 弘範將命入城，數其大臣之罪，皆屈服，竟取稱臣降表來上。

translations.literal: Hongfan bore orders and entered the city, reckoning the crimes of its great ministers; all submitted; in the end he took the memorial of submission calling themselves subjects and brought it up.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan entered the city on imperial orders, condemned the Song ministers until they yielded, and at last secured a full surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 十三年，台州叛，討平之，誅其為首者而已。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Taizhou rebelled; he suppressed and pacified it, executing only those who had led it.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen he put down a revolt in Taizhou, executing only the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 十四年，師還，授鎮國上將軍、江東道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the army returned; he was appointed General Who Guards the State and Pacification Commissioner of the Jiangdong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned in year fourteen, he was made General Who Guards the State and Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，宋張世傑立廣王昞于海上，閩、廣響應，俾弘範往平之，授蒙古漢軍都元帥。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Song's Zhang Shijie set up Prince Guang Bing on the sea; Fujian and Guangdong responded; Hongfan was ordered to go pacify them and was appointed Grand Marshal of Mongol and Han Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen Zhang Shijie crowned Prince Guang Bing at sea; Fujian and Guangdong rallied, and Hongfan was sent to crush them as Grand Marshal of Mongol and Han forces.

sentences.zh: 陛辭奏曰：「漢人無統蒙古軍者，乞以蒙古信臣為首帥。」

translations.literal: At audience on departure he memorialized, saying: 'No Han person commands Mongol armies; I beg that a trusted Mongol minister be made chief commander.'
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave of the throne, he asked that a trusted Mongol officer lead, since no Han commander had ever held Mongol troops.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝知而父與察罕之事乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Do you know the affair of your father and Chaghan?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether he knew what had happened between his father and Chaghan.

sentences.zh: 其破安豐也，汝父欲留兵守之，察罕不從。

translations.literal: When they broke Anfeng, your father wished to leave troops to guard it, but Chaghan did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At Anfeng his father had wanted to leave a garrison, but Chaghan refused.

sentences.zh: 師既南，安豐復為宋有，進退幾失據，汝父深悔恨，良由委任不專故也，豈可使汝復有汝父之悔乎。

translations.literal: Once the army had gone south, Anfeng again belonged to Song; advance and retreat nearly lost footing; your father deeply regretted it—truly because delegated authority was not exclusive; how could one let you again have your father's regret?
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched south, Anfeng fell back to Song and the campaign nearly lost its footing; his father bitterly regretted divided command—shall I let you repeat that mistake?

sentences.zh: 今付汝大事，能以汝父之心為心，則予汝嘉。」

translations.literal: Now I entrust you with a great matter; if you can take your father's heart as your heart, then I will grant you praise.'
translations.idiomatic: I now give you full command; serve with your father's steadfastness, and you will have my favor.

sentences.zh: 面賜錦衣、玉帶，弘範不受，以劍甲為請。

translations.literal: In person he bestowed brocade robes and a jade belt; Hongfan did not accept them and requested sword and armor instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally granted brocade and a jade belt, but Hongfan declined them and asked for sword and armor instead.

sentences.zh: 帝出武庫劍甲，聽其自擇，且諭之曰：「劍，汝之副也，不用令者，以此處之。」

translations.literal: The emperor brought out sword and armor from the weapons store and let him choose for himself, and additionally instructed him, saying: 'The sword is your deputy; whoever disobeys orders—deal with him by this.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brought arms from the imperial arsenal for him to choose and said, 'This sword is your deputy—use it on any man who disobeys.'

sentences.zh: 將行，薦李恒為己貳，從之。

translations.literal: About to depart, he recommended Li Heng as his second-in-command; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched, he recommended Li Heng as his second, and the appointment was granted.

sentences.zh: 至揚州，選將校水陸二萬，分道南征，以弟弘正為先鋒，戒之曰：「選汝驍勇，非私汝也。

translations.literal: Reaching Yangzhou, he selected officers and commanders, twenty thousand by land and water, and marched south by separate routes; he made his younger brother Hongzheng vanguard and admonished him, saying: 'You were chosen for your fierceness and bravery—it is not favoritism toward you.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou he picked twenty thousand land and sea troops and marched south in columns, making his brother Hongzheng vanguard and warning him, 'You lead because you are brave—not because you are my brother.

sentences.zh: 軍法重，我不敢以私撓公，勉之。」

translations.literal: Military law is weighty; I dare not let private feeling bend public duty—strive hard.'
translations.idiomatic: Military law is strict; I will not let kinship bend justice—do your duty.'

sentences.zh: 弘正所向克捷。

translations.literal: Wherever Hongzheng went, he conquered with success.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng won wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 進攻三江寨，寨據隘乘高，不可近，因連兵向之，寨中持滿以待。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Sanjiang Stockade, the stockade held a narrow pass and exploited the heights and could not be approached; therefore he massed troops and moved toward it; inside the stockade they held bows fully drawn awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanjiang Stockade the defenders held the heights at a narrow pass; Hongfan massed troops before it while archers inside stood at full draw.

sentences.zh: 弘範下令下馬治朝食，若將持久者。

translations.literal: Hongfan gave the order to dismount and prepare the morning meal, as if intending a prolonged stay.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan ordered his men to dismount and eat breakfast as though settling in for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 持滿者疑不敢動，而他寨不虞也。

translations.literal: Those holding full draw doubted and did not dare move, while the other stockades did not anticipate.
translations.idiomatic: The drawn bows held their fire in uncertainty, while the other stockades remained unsuspecting.

sentences.zh: 忽麾軍連拔數寨，迴擣三江，盡拔之。

translations.literal: Suddenly he waved the army to capture several stockades in succession, wheeled back to strike Sanjiang, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he swept several stockades, then wheeled back and took Sanjiang as well.

sentences.zh: 至漳州，軍其東門，命別將攻南門、西門，乃乘虛破其北門，拔之。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhangzhou, he encamped at its east gate, ordered other generals to attack the south and west gates, then exploited the gap to break the north gate and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangzhou he pinned the east gate, sent others against south and west, then broke through the undefended north gate and took the city.

sentences.zh: 攻鮑浦寨，又拔之。

translations.literal: Attacking Baopu Stockade, he captured it again.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Baopu Stockade and took that too.

sentences.zh: 由是瀕海郡邑皆望風降附。

translations.literal: From this, coastal commanderies and counties all, at sight of the wind, surrendered and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After that, coastal towns surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 獲宋丞相文天祥于五坡嶺，使之拜，不屈，弘範義之，待以賓禮，送至京師。

translations.literal: He captured Song Chancellor Wen Tianxiang at Wupo Ridge; he made him bow; Wen would not submit; Hongfan honored his righteousness and treated him with guest rites, sending him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Song Chancellor Wen Tianxiang at Wupo Ridge; when ordered to bow, Wen refused; Hongfan admired his integrity, treated him as an honored guest, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 獲宋禮部侍郎鄧光薦，命子珪師事之。

translations.literal: He captured Song Vice Minister of Rites Deng Guangjian and ordered his son Gui to take him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Song Vice Minister of Rites Deng Guangjian and had his son Gui study under him.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月庚戌，由潮陽港發舶入海，至甲子門，獲宋斥候將劉青、顧凱，乃知廣王所在。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the first month of the sixteenth year, he launched ships from Chaoyang Harbor into the sea, reached Jiazi Gate, captured Song scout generals Liu Qing and Gu Kai, and thus learned where Prince Guang was.
translations.idiomatic: On the first month, day gengxu of year sixteen, he sailed from Chaoyang Harbor, reached Jiazi Gate, captured scouts Liu Qing and Gu Kai, and learned the young emperor's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，次崖山。

translations.literal: On xinyou, he halted at Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinyou he anchored off Yamen.

sentences.zh: 宋軍千餘艘碇海中，建樓櫓其上，隱然堅壁也，弘範引舟師赴之。

translations.literal: More than a thousand Song warships were moored in the sea; tower and fighting platforms were built upon them, resembling a firm wall; Hongfan led the fleet toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand Song ships lay at anchor with towers built on deck like a floating fortress; Hongfan led his fleet against them.

sentences.zh: 崖山東西對峙，其北水淺，舟膠，非潮來不可進，乃由山之東轉南入大洋，始得逼其舟，又出奇兵斷其汲路，燒其宮室。

translations.literal: Yamen faced east and west across from each other; to the north the water was shallow and ships grounded; only when the tide came could one advance; therefore he rounded from the east of the mountain and turned south into the open sea, and only then could he press upon their ships; he also sent a surprise force to cut their route for drawing water and burned their palace buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Yamen's cliffs faced each other east and west; shoals to the north grounded ships unless the tide was in, so Hongfan swung south around the eastern point into open water, closed on the fleet, cut off their water supply with a flanking force, and burned their palaces.

sentences.zh: 世傑有甥在弘範軍中，三使招之，世傑不從。

translations.literal: Shijie had a nephew in Hongfan's army; three times messengers were sent to summon him; Shijie would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie's nephew was in Hongfan's camp; three times Hongfan sent him to summon Shijie, but Shijie refused.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，李恒自廣州至，授以戰艦二，使守北面。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Li Heng arrived from Guangzhou; two warships were entrusted to him and he was made to guard the north face.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiaxu, Li Heng arrived from Guangzhou with two warships and was posted to block the north.

sentences.zh: 二月癸未，將戰，或請先用砲。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the second month, about to give battle, someone requested using cannon first.
translations.idiomatic: On the second month, day guiwei, as battle neared, someone proposed opening with cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 弘範曰：「火起則舟散，不如戰也。」

translations.literal: Hongfan said: 'If fire rises, the ships will scatter; it is better to fight.'
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan said fire would scatter the fleet—better to fight ship to ship.

sentences.zh: 明日，四分其軍，軍其東南北三面，弘範自將一軍相去里餘，下令曰：「宋舟潮至必東遁，急攻之，勿令得去，聞吾樂作乃戰，違令者斬。」

translations.literal: The next day, he divided his army into four parts, encamping on the east, south, and north faces; Hongfan personally commanded one army a little more than a li distant, giving the order: 'When the tide comes, Song ships will surely flee east—attack urgently and do not let them escape; when you hear my music begin, then fight; whoever violates the order shall be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day he quartered his force on three sides while he held a separate command a li away, ordering, 'When the tide turns the Song ships will run east—strike hard and do not let them escape; attack only when my music sounds; disobey and die.'

sentences.zh: 先麾北面一軍乘潮而戰，不克，李恒等順潮而退。

translations.literal: First he waved the northern army to fight riding the tide; they did not prevail; Li Heng and others withdrew with the tide.
translations.idiomatic: First the northern wing attacked with the tide but failed, and Li Heng withdrew with the ebb.

sentences.zh: 樂作，宋將以為且宴，少懈，弘範舟師犯其前，衆繼之。

translations.literal: The music began; Song generals thought it was about to be a banquet and relaxed somewhat; Hongfan's fleet struck their front; the masses followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the music started, Song commanders thought it signaled a feast and slackened; Hongfan's fleet struck their front and the rest followed.

sentences.zh: 豫構戰樓於舟尾，以布幙障之，命將士負盾而伏，令之曰：「聞金聲起戰，先金而妄動者死。」

translations.literal: Battle towers were pre-built on the sterns of ships, screened with cloth curtains; officers and soldiers were ordered to carry shields and lie concealed; he commanded them: 'When you hear the gold sound, rise to fight; whoever moves rashly before the gold—death.'
translations.idiomatic: He had fighting towers built on the sterns, screened with canvas, and ordered his men to crouch behind shields until the brass signal sounded—anyone who moved early would die.

sentences.zh: 飛矢集如蝟，伏盾者不動。

translations.literal: Flying arrows gathered thick as a hedgehog; those hiding behind shields did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows fell thick as porcupine quills, but the men behind their shields held fast.

sentences.zh: 舟將接，鳴金撤障，弓弩火石交作，頃刻并破七舟，宋師大潰。

translations.literal: As the ships were about to meet, the gold was sounded, the screens were removed, bows, crossbows, and fire stones worked together; in an instant seven ships were broken together; the Song army was greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: As the ships closed, the signal sounded, the screens dropped, and bows, crossbows, and fire bombs rained down; in moments seven ships were smashed and the Song fleet collapsed.

sentences.zh: 宋臣抱其主昞赴水死。

translations.literal: Song ministers embraced their lord Bing and went into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: Song ministers carried the young emperor Bing into the water and drowned with him.

sentences.zh: 獲其符璽印章。

translations.literal: His tally seals and imperial seals were captured.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the imperial seals and regalia.

sentences.zh: 世傑先遁，李恒追至大洋不及。

translations.literal: Shijie fled first; Li Heng pursued to the open sea but did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie escaped first; Li Heng chased him into open water but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 世傑走交趾，風壞舟，死海陵港。

translations.literal: Shijie fled toward Jiaozhi; wind wrecked his ship; he died at Hailing Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie fled toward Annam, but a storm wrecked his ship and he died at Hailing Harbor.

sentences.zh: 其餘將吏皆降。

translations.literal: The remaining generals and officials all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining commanders and officials all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 嶺海悉平，磨崖山之陽，勒石紀功而還。

translations.literal: The Ling region and the sea were entirely pacified; on the sunny face of Yamen Mountain he carved stone to record achievement and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The south was fully pacified; he inscribed his victory on the cliffs of Yamen and returned.

sentences.zh: 十月，入朝，賜宴內殿，慰勞甚厚。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he entered court audience; a banquet was granted in the inner hall and consolation and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he went to court, was feasted in the inner palace, and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，瘴癘疾作，帝命尚醫診視，遣近臣臨議用藥，敕衛士監門，止雜人毋擾其病。

translations.literal: Before long, miasmic fever illness set in; the emperor ordered the Court Physician to examine and treat him, sent a close minister to attend and consult on medicine, and commanded guard soldiers to watch the gate, stopping miscellaneous persons from disturbing his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon malarial fever struck; the emperor sent court physicians, dispatched a close adviser to oversee his care, and posted guards to keep visitors away.

sentences.zh: 病甚，沐浴易衣冠，扶掖至中庭，面闕再拜。

translations.literal: When the illness was severe, he bathed and changed robe and cap, was supported to the central courtyard, and bowed twice facing the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, he bathed, dressed in formal robes, was helped into the courtyard, and bowed twice toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 退坐，命酒作樂，與親故言別。

translations.literal: He withdrew and sat, ordered wine and had music made, and took leave in words with kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: He returned indoors, called for wine and music, and said farewell to family and friends.

sentences.zh: 出所賜劍甲，命付嗣子珪曰：「汝父以是立功，汝佩服勿忘也。」

translations.literal: He brought out the sword and armor that had been bestowed and ordered them given to his heir Gui, saying: 'Your father by these achieved merit; you—wear and keep them—do not forget.'
translations.idiomatic: He produced the sword and armor the emperor had given him and told his heir Gui, 'Your father won glory with these—wear them and never forget.'

sentences.zh: 語竟，端坐而卒。

translations.literal: When the words were finished, he sat upright and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking, he sat upright and died.

sentences.zh: 年四十三。

translations.literal: His age was forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 贈銀青榮祿大夫、平章政事，諡武烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Silver-Girdled Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and Grand Councillor; his posthumous title was Martial Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Silver-Girdled Grand Master and Grand Councillor, with the temple name Martial Fierce.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，加贈推忠效節翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、齊國公，改諡忠武。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide, additional posthumous grants were made: Merit Worthy of Loyal Devotion and Steadfast Conduct, Assisting the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, Upper Pillar of the State, Duke of Qi; the posthumous title was changed to Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 4 he was further ennobled as Loyal Merit Assisting the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Qi, and Second Rank Equivalent; his posthumous name became Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，加保大功臣，加封淮陽王，諡獻武。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou, he was added Merit of Protecting the Great, enfeoffed additionally as Prince of Huaiyang; posthumous title Offered Martial.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 6 he was made Merit Protector of the Dynasty, created Prince of Huaiyang, with the posthumous name Offered Martial.

sentences.zh: 子珪，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Gui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui has a separate biography.
